cloud/api-and-mcp.title: API and MCP
cloud/api-and-mcp.description: Call Stirling Cloud from your own code with an API key, or connect an AI assistant over MCP.
cloud/api-and-mcp.markdown:
Run PDF tools from your own scripts, or let an AI assistant such as Claude use them over MCP. Guests can't use the API or MCP, so [create an account](doc:cloud/account) first.

## Get an API key

- **Team owners:** open **Settings → Preferences → API Keys** and select **Create key**. Copy the secret straight away, as it is shown only once. **Revoke key** stops a key working immediately.
- **Members:** open **Settings → Developer → API Keys** to copy your personal key. To replace it, select the refresh button and confirm with **Refresh Keys**.

To make requests with your key, see [REST API](doc:developers/api).

API calls use team credits ([Plans, credits and billing](doc:cloud/plans-and-billing)).

## Connect an AI assistant (MCP)

1. Open **Settings → Developer → MCP Server** and copy **Your MCP endpoint**.
2. Under **Connect your AI assistant**, pick your client and paste the snippet into the file shown.
3. Restart the client. On first use, sign in to Stirling and select **Allow access**.

There is no key to copy. The assistant runs as your account and uses credits. See [Connect an AI assistant](doc:mcp/connect).

cloud/account.title: Account and sign-in
cloud/account.description: Sign in to Stirling Cloud or use it as a guest, and manage your password, sign-out and account deletion.
cloud/account.markdown:
## Sign in

Go to [stirling.com/app](https://stirling.com/app) and enter your email and password, or choose **Sign in with Google**, **Sign in with GitHub** or **Use magic link instead** (Stirling emails you a sign-in link).

To use the same account in the desktop app, see [Connection modes](doc:desktop/connection-modes).

## Create an account

Select **Create an account** on the sign-in page. Sign up with Google or GitHub, or with your email and a password of at least 6 characters, then open the confirmation link if one is emailed to you.

## Reset your password

Select **Forgot your password?** on the sign-in page. Enter your email and select **Send reset link**, then follow the link in the email.

## Use Stirling as a guest

Select **Skip →** on the sign-in page. Guests can use every manual PDF tool. AI tools, automation, the Processor, API keys, MCP and saving files to Stirling Cloud need an account.

To keep a guest account, open **Settings → Account Settings → Overview**, fill in **Upgrade Guest Account** and select **Upgrade Account**.

## Change your password

Open **Settings → Account Settings → Passwords & Security** and select **Change password**.

## Sign out

Open **Settings → Account Settings → Overview** and select **Log out**.

## Delete your account

Open **Settings → Account Settings → Overview**, select **Delete Account**, type your email address and select **Delete My Account**. Deletion is permanent. Guest accounts do not have this option.

cloud/cloud.title: Stirling Cloud
cloud/cloud.description: Use Stirling PDF in your browser at stirling.com/app, with nothing to install or maintain.
cloud/cloud.markdown:
Stirling Cloud is Stirling PDF hosted for you at [stirling.com/app](https://stirling.com/app). Sign in, or select **Skip →** to try it as a guest ([Account and sign-in](doc:cloud/account)).

Your avatar at the bottom of the left bar opens **Settings** for your account, team, API keys and billing.

Manual tools are free. Automation, AI and API calls use credits ([Plans, credits and billing](doc:cloud/plans-and-billing)).


Sign-in options, guest mode and deleting your account.
Invite people and share a plan.
Credits, spend caps and invoices.
Where your files go and how long they are kept.
What is different on Cloud.
Call Stirling from code or an AI assistant.


To learn the tools, see the [User guide](doc:tools/tools).

cloud/files-and-privacy.title: Files and privacy
cloud/files-and-privacy.description: Where Stirling Cloud processes and stores your files, what AI tools send, and how long data is kept.
cloud/files-and-privacy.markdown:
## Where your files are processed

| What you do | Where it happens |
|---|---|
| View, read, rearrange pages, manage files in your workspace | In your browser. The file stays on your device. |
| Server tools such as compress, OCR, convert and watermark | Sent to Stirling's servers, processed and returned. |
| AI tools and the AI assistant | Stirling's servers, plus an AI provider for the text the feature needs. |
| Processor pipelines | Stirling's servers, reading from and writing to the storage you connect. |

Files you open in the editor stay in your browser's storage until you remove them. They are saved to Stirling Cloud only if you are signed in and choose to upload or share them. Share links open only for signed-in users ([My files and sharing](doc:tools/workspace/files-and-sharing)).

## What AI tools send

AI features use Anthropic (Claude) models and Voyage AI embeddings. They receive prompts and the text or excerpts the feature needs, never whole files. Neither provider uses your data to train models.

## Storage and retention

- Stirling Cloud runs on Amazon Web Services, and stored files are encrypted at rest.
- Files you save to Stirling Cloud stay there until you delete them or your account.
- Card payments go to Stripe. Stirling never stores your card details.

For the full terms, see the [privacy policy](https://stirling.com/legal/privacy-policy) and the [list of subprocessors](https://stirling.com/legal/subprocessors).

cloud/plans-and-billing.title: Plans, credits and billing
cloud/plans-and-billing.description: What uses credits on Stirling Cloud, what happens at the limit, and how team owners turn on paid processing and manage billing.
cloud/plans-and-billing.markdown:
Manual PDF tools on Stirling Cloud are free. Automation, AI and API calls use credits from your team's monthly allowance, and after that the team owner can turn on pay-as-you-go. Prices are on [stirling.com/pricing](https://stirling.com/pricing).

## What uses credits

| Work | Credits |
|---|---|
| Tools you run yourself in the editor and reader | Free |
| **[Automate](doc:tools/guides/automate)** runs, Processor pipelines and policies, [processing folders](doc:tools/workspace/processing-folders) | Yes |
| AI tools and the AI assistant | Yes |
| API calls and MCP actions | Yes |

- Each file processed uses one credit. Very long or very large files can use more.
- A file run through several steps of one automation counts once.
- If a job fails on its first step, the credit is returned.
- The free allowance belongs to the team and resets each month. **Free credits** in the sidebar shows what is left.

## When the team hits its limit

Manual tools keep working. Automations, pipelines and AI tools pause, and API calls return HTTP `402` with `PAYG_LIMIT_REACHED`.

## Where to manage billing

Only the team owner can change the plan, in **Settings → Workspace → Usage & Billing**. Members see a read-only view in **Settings → Billing → Plan**. In the desktop app, select **Open Usage & Billing in browser**.

## Turn on the Processor plan

The Processor plan is pay-as-you-go for everything that uses credits, up to a monthly spend limit you choose.

1. In **Usage & Billing**, on the **Processor** row, select **Switch on the Processor**.
2. Choose **Pay as you go**, set your monthly spend limit and select **Continue to payment**.

To change the limit, select **Raise limit** on the **Processor** row and **Save limit**.

Or choose **Prepay a year** to buy 12 months of credits at a discount, by card or bank transfer. Prepaid credits are used first and expire after 12 months.

## Upgrade to Team or add users

A free team holds up to 5 people. The Team plan adds users in blocks of 100.

1. In **Usage & Billing**, select **Compare plans → Upgrade to Team**, or **Add capacity** on the **Users** row.
2. Choose **Monthly** or **Yearly** and the number of users, then select **Continue to payment**.

For data residency or SCIM, select **Get an enterprise quote**. Single sign-on through your own identity provider needs a self-hosted server ([OAuth2 / OIDC single sign-on](doc:server/security/oauth-sso)).

## Payment, invoices and cancelling

- **Payment method → Update** opens the Stripe billing portal.
- **Invoices** lists every invoice.
- On a paid plan, **Manage subscription** opens the Stripe portal, where you can also cancel.

cloud/processor-and-ai.title: Processor and AI on Cloud
cloud/processor-and-ai.description: Who can open the Processor on Stirling Cloud, what differs from a self-hosted server, and how AI tools are billed.
cloud/processor-and-ai.markdown:
For how the Processor and AI tools work, see [Processor](doc:processor/processor) and [AI assistant](doc:tools/guides/ai-assistant).

## Open the Processor

Select **Processor** in the left bar. The team owner can open it, including you on your own personal team. Invited members see **Ask an admin for processor access**, and guests are asked to create an account. See [Setup and access](doc:processor/setup-and-access).

To build your first pipeline, see [Create your first pipeline](doc:processor/getting-started).

## What is different on Cloud

Stirling Cloud has no **Folder** sources or destinations and no **Custom API** integrations ([Sources](doc:processor/sources), [Integrations](doc:processor/integrations)).

## AI on Cloud

AI tools are on for every signed-in account. AI requests, pipelines and policies use team credits and pause at the limit ([Plans, credits and billing](doc:cloud/plans-and-billing)). For what AI providers receive, see [Files and privacy](doc:cloud/files-and-privacy).

cloud/teams.title: Teams
cloud/teams.description: How Stirling Cloud teams share a plan and credits, and how owners invite, remove and hand over members or connect servers.
cloud/teams.markdown:
Every Stirling Cloud account belongs to a team, which shares one plan and credit allowance. When you sign up you get a personal team with just you in it.

## Owners and members

| | Team owner | Member |
|---|---|---|
| Use every tool, AI and the API | Yes | Yes |
| Open the Processor | Yes | No |
| Invite and remove members, rename the team | Yes | No |
| Manage the plan, spend cap and invoices | Yes | No |
| Approve self-hosted servers | Yes | No |
| Leave the team | After handing over ownership | Yes |

Owners manage the team in **Settings → Workspace → Users**. Members see it under **Settings → Account Settings → Users**. In the desktop app it is under **Settings → Team**.

## Invite members

Select **Invite people**, enter the email address and select **Send invite**.

The person signs in or creates an account with the invited address, then selects **Accept** on the banner.

- Invitations expire after 7 days. Withdraw one with **Cancel invitation**.
- You can't invite someone who pays for their own subscription.
- A free team holds up to 5 people. For more, [upgrade to Team](doc:cloud/plans-and-billing).

## Leave or remove

- **Members:** select **Leave Team** to return to your personal team.
- **Owners:** select **Remove from team** on a member. They keep their account but lose access to the team.

If a team has no owner, a member can select **Become team owner**.

## Transfer ownership

Select **Transfer ownership** on the member and confirm. You become a member. The plan and credits stay with the team.

If the team has connected self-hosted servers, start the transfer on the server instead: open **Settings → Workspace → Users** there and change the recipient's role to **Organisation Owner**.

## Connected self-hosted servers

A self-hosted server can share your team's processing allowance. Its admin starts the link from the server ([Connect to Stirling Cloud](doc:server/licensing/connect-to-stirling-cloud)), which opens **Connect this server?** on Stirling Cloud. The team owner approves it:

1. Check that the **Address** is your server.
2. Tick **I recognise this address and want to connect it to my team** and select **Connect server**.

**Settings → Workspace → Connected instances** lists connected servers. **Remove connection** revokes a server's access to your team.

desktop/connection-modes.title: Connection modes
desktop/connection-modes.description: Switch the desktop app between Local Only, Stirling Cloud and Self-Hosted modes, and connect it to your organisation's server.
desktop/connection-modes.markdown:
The connection mode decides where your tools run and which account you use. Change the mode in **Settings → Connection Mode** (select the account row at the bottom of the left sidebar to open Settings).

| Mode | Sign-in | Where tools run |
|---|---|---|
| **Local Only** | None | On your computer. Tools that need a server are blocked. |
| **Stirling Cloud** | Your Stirling account | On your computer when possible, otherwise in Stirling Cloud. |
| **Self-Hosted** | An account on your organisation's server | On that server. |

See [Where your tools run](doc:desktop/where-tools-run) for details.

## Local Only

You get this mode if you select **Continue without signing in** on first launch, or log out.

## Sign in to Stirling Cloud

1. Go to **Settings → Connection Mode** and select **Sign In**.
2. On **Sign in to Stirling**, choose **Google** or **GitHub** (finish in your browser), or enter your email and password under **Or continue with email** and select **Login**.

Once signed in, Settings also shows **Workspace** and **Team**. See [Account and sign-in](doc:cloud/account).

## Connect to a self-hosted server

You need the server's address and an account on it. The server must have login turned on, otherwise the app shows **Login Not Enabled** ([Sign-in and security](doc:server/security/sign-in-and-security)).

1. Go to **Settings → Connection Mode** and select **Sign In**.
2. Select **or connect to a self-hosted account**.
3. In **Server URL**, enter the full address, including the port if there is one, for example `https://pdf.example.com` or `http://192.168.1.53:8080`.
4. Select **Continue**.
5. On **Sign in to Server**, enter your username and password, or use single sign-on.

On macOS, allow the **Local Network** prompt the first time you connect to a server on your network.

## Switch modes or sign out

Select **Log Out** in **Settings → Connection Mode** to return to Local Only. To move between Stirling Cloud and a server, log out, then sign in with the other option.

desktop/files.title: Opening and saving files
desktop/files.description: Open PDFs in the desktop app, make it your default PDF app, save changes back to disk and use more than one window.
desktop/files.markdown:
## Open files

- Double-click a PDF, or right-click it and choose **Open with → Stirling PDF**.
- In the app, select **Open from computer** in the left sidebar.
- Drag files onto the app window.

Files you open stay in the app until you remove them.

## Make Stirling PDF your default PDF app

Go to **Settings → Preferences → Editor defaults** and select **Set as Default**. On Windows this opens **Default apps** in Windows Settings, where you pick Stirling PDF for PDF files.

## Save your changes

Select **Save** in the top bar, or press **Ctrl+S** (**Cmd+S** on macOS), to write over the file you opened. Use **Save As** for a copy.

Closing a window with unsaved changes asks whether to save first.

If another program changes an open file while you have unsaved edits, **File changed on disk** asks you to choose **Keep my changes** or **Use the disk version**.

## Work in more than one window

Press **Ctrl+N** (**Cmd+N** on macOS) for a new window, or choose **Open in new window** from a file's menu in the **File library**. Windows and macOS only.

See [Desktop app shortcuts](doc:tools/workspace/keyboard-shortcuts) for more shortcuts.

desktop/install.title: Install the desktop app
desktop/install.description: Download and install Stirling PDF Desktop on Windows, macOS or Linux, including winget, Scoop, Homebrew and AUR, and what happens on first launch.
desktop/install.markdown: Requires Windows 10 or 11. **Installer (x64)** 1. Download [Stirling-PDF-windows-x86_64.msi](https://files.stirlingpdf.com/win-installer.exe). 2. Run it and approve the administrator prompt. It installs for all users. 3. Open **Stirling PDF** from the Start menu. **winget (x64)** ```powershell winget install StirlingTools.StirlingPDF ``` **Scoop (x64)** ```powershell scoop bucket add stirling-pdf https://github.com/Stirling-Tools/homebrew-stirling-pdf scoop install stirling-pdf/stirling-pdf ``` Update with `scoop update stirling-pdf`. **Windows on ARM** Download [Stirling-PDF-windows-arm64-setup.exe](https://github.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-PDF/releases/latest/download/Stirling-PDF-windows-arm64-setup.exe) and run it. The ARM build isn't on winget. If the app runs but no window appears, install the [Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime](https://developer.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/webview2/) and start it again. Requires macOS 10.15 or later, on Apple silicon or Intel. **DMG** 1. Download [Stirling PDF for Mac](https://files.stirlingpdf.com/mac-installer.dmg). 2. Open the DMG and drag **Stirling PDF** into **Applications**. 3. Open **Stirling PDF** from Applications. If macOS blocks the app, open **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, select **Open Anyway** next to the Stirling PDF message, then open it again. **Homebrew** ```bash brew tap stirling-tools/stirling-pdf brew install --cask stirling-pdf ``` Requires a 64-bit x86 (x86_64) system. **Debian and Ubuntu (.deb)** ```bash wget https://files.stirlingpdf.com/linux-installer.deb sudo apt install ./linux-installer.deb ``` **Fedora and RHEL (.rpm)** ```bash wget https://files.stirlingpdf.com/linux-installer.rpm sudo dnf install ./linux-installer.rpm ``` **AppImage** (no install needed) ```bash wget https://files.stirlingpdf.com/linux-installer.AppImage chmod +x linux-installer.AppImage ./linux-installer.AppImage ``` **Arch Linux (AUR)** ```bash paru -S stirling-pdf-desktop ``` ## First launch On first launch, **Sign in to Stirling** gives three choices: - Sign in to use [Stirling Cloud](doc:desktop/connection-modes). - Select **or connect to a self-hosted account** to use [your organisation's server](doc:desktop/connection-modes). - Select **Continue without signing in** to work in Local Only mode. You can change this later in **Settings → Connection Mode**. If a tool says **Backend starting up...**, wait a few seconds. To install silently or pre-configure many machines, see [Managed deployment](doc:desktop/managed-deployment).

desktop/managed-deployment.title: Managed deployment
desktop/managed-deployment.description: Pre-configure and lock the Stirling PDF desktop app on many machines with Intune, Jamf, SCCM, Group Policy or any other deployment tool.
desktop/managed-deployment.markdown:
Use a provisioning file to roll out the desktop app pre-configured: point every machine at your self-hosted server, stop users changing it, and control updates.

Your server must have login turned on, with an account or single sign-on for each user ([Sign-in and security](doc:server/security/sign-in-and-security)).

## Where the file goes

At every launch the app looks for `stirling-provisioning.json`, first in the user folder and then in the system folder, and applies the first one it finds:

| OS | System folder | User folder |
|---|---|---|
| Windows | `%PROGRAMDATA%\Stirling-PDF\` | `%APPDATA%\Stirling-PDF\` |
| macOS | `/Library/Application Support/Stirling-PDF/` | `~/Library/Application Support/Stirling-PDF/` |
| Linux | `/etc/stirling-pdf/` | `~/.config/Stirling-PDF/` |

- **System file:** stays in place and is applied at every launch. Use this for managed fleets.
- **User file:** applied once, then deleted. It can't lock the update setting.

## The provisioning file

Every field is optional:

```json
{
  "serverUrl": "https://pdf.example.com",
  "lockConnectionMode": true,
  "updateMode": "disabled"
}
```

| Field | Type | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `serverUrl` | string | Your self-hosted server, including `http://` or `https://` and the port if needed. Sets Self-Hosted mode. Stirling Cloud mode can't be provisioned. |
| `lockConnectionMode` | boolean | `true` stops users connecting to a different server or to Stirling Cloud. Only applies when `serverUrl` is set. Users can still choose **Use local tools instead**. |
| `loginAgreementEnabled` | boolean | `true` turns on the login agreement dialog. Works without `serverUrl`. See the note below. |
| `updateMode` | string | `prompt` (default) asks before installing, `auto` installs updates at startup, `disabled` never checks. |

> **📝 Note: Login agreement text**
>
> `loginAgreementEnabled` only switches the dialog on. With no text, nothing is shown. When connected to a server, the server supplies the text ([Sign-in and security](doc:server/security/sign-in-and-security)). For Local Only use, save the text as Markdown in `customFiles/disclaimer/` inside the user folder above, for example `customFiles/disclaimer/en.md`.


On all-users Windows installs the app can't update itself, so use `updateMode: "disabled"` and push new versions with your deployment tool.

## Windows (Intune, SCCM, Group Policy)

The x64 MSI accepts these properties and writes the provisioning file for you:

| Property | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `STIRLING_SERVER_URL` | Server URL | `https://pdf.example.com` |
| `STIRLING_LOCK_CONNECTION` | Lock the connection (`1`, `true`, `yes` or `y`) | `1` |
| `STIRLING_LOGIN_AGREEMENT` | Turn on the login agreement dialog (`1`, `true`, `yes` or `y`) | `1` |
| `STIRLING_UPDATE_MODE` | `prompt`, `auto` or `disabled`. An invalid value makes the install fail. | `disabled` |
| `INSTALLDIR` | Custom install folder | `C:\CustomPath\Stirling PDF` |
| `ALLUSERS` | Install for all users | `1` |

```batch
msiexec /i "Stirling-PDF-windows-x86_64.msi" /qn ^
  STIRLING_SERVER_URL="https://pdf.example.com" ^
  STIRLING_LOCK_CONNECTION=1 ^
  STIRLING_UPDATE_MODE=disabled ^
  ALLUSERS=1
```

With winget:

```powershell
winget install StirlingTools.StirlingPDF `
  --custom "STIRLING_SERVER_URL=https://pdf.example.com STIRLING_LOCK_CONNECTION=1 STIRLING_UPDATE_MODE=disabled"
```

The MSI is [Stirling-PDF-windows-x86_64.msi](https://files.stirlingpdf.com/win-installer.exe). An all-users install writes the system file. The Windows on ARM installer accepts none of these properties, so deploy the JSON file to `%PROGRAMDATA%\Stirling-PDF\` instead.

## macOS (Jamf, MDM)

Push the file to `/Library/Application Support/Stirling-PDF/stirling-provisioning.json`.

## Linux

Write the file to `/etc/stirling-pdf/stirling-provisioning.json`.

## Changing or removing managed settings

The app keeps provisioned values and locks after the file is gone, so don't rely on deleting the file.

- **Change the server or lock:** deploy an updated system file with `serverUrl` and the `lockConnectionMode` you want, then restart the app.
- **Reset a user completely:** quit the app and delete that user's `stirling.pdf.dev` folders ([Data and log locations](doc:desktop/updates-and-data)). A system file is applied again at the next launch.

desktop/updates-and-data.title: Updates, data and uninstall
desktop/updates-and-data.description: How the desktop app updates itself, where it keeps its data and logs on each system, and how to remove it completely.
desktop/updates-and-data.markdown:
## Updates

Shortly after it starts, the app checks for a new version. If there is one, **Update Available** appears:

- **Install Now** installs it. Then select **Restart Now**.
- **Later** hides the prompt for a day.
- **Download Latest** opens the download if the app can't install the update itself.

On Windows (x64) the app is installed for all users, so the prompt usually shows **Administrator permissions required**. Select **Download Latest** and run the installer, or run `winget upgrade StirlingTools.StirlingPDF` from an administrator terminal.

To change how updates work, go to **Settings → Preferences → Software Updates → Update behavior**:

- **Ask me before installing updates** (default)
- **Install updates automatically**
- **Don't check for updates**

If **Software Updates** shows **Managed by administrator**, or isn't there, your IT team controls updates ([Managed deployment](doc:desktop/managed-deployment)).

If you installed with a package manager, you can also update with it:

```bash
winget upgrade StirlingTools.StirlingPDF   # Windows
brew upgrade --cask stirling-tools/stirling-pdf/stirling-pdf   # macOS
paru -Syu                                  # Arch Linux (AUR)
```

## Data and log locations




| Folder | What's in it |
|---|---|
| `%APPDATA%\Stirling-PDF` | Engine data and logs (`logs\`) |
| `%APPDATA%\stirling.pdf.dev` | Connection mode, server address and update setting |
| `%LOCALAPPDATA%\stirling.pdf.dev` | Workspace files and app logs (`logs\`) |

Sign-in tokens are kept in Windows Credential Manager.




| Folder | What's in it |
|---|---|
| `~/Library/Application Support/Stirling-PDF` | Engine data and logs (`logs/`) |
| `~/Library/Application Support/stirling.pdf.dev` | Connection mode, server address and update setting |
| `~/Library/WebKit/stirling.pdf.dev` | Workspace files |
| `~/Library/Logs/Stirling-PDF` and `~/Library/Logs/stirling.pdf.dev` | App logs |

Sign-in tokens are kept in Keychain.




| Folder | What's in it |
|---|---|
| `~/.config/Stirling-PDF` | Engine data and logs (`logs/`) |
| `~/.local/share/stirling.pdf.dev` | Connection mode, server address, update setting, workspace files and app logs (`logs/`) |




To report a problem, zip the log folders and attach them to a GitHub issue ([How do I report a bug or ask for a feature?](doc:tools/faq)), with the **Desktop Version** from **Settings → Preferences → Software Updates**.

## Uninstall




Open Windows **Settings → Apps → Installed apps**, find **Stirling PDF** and select **Uninstall**. Or run `winget uninstall StirlingTools.StirlingPDF`.




Quit the app and drag **Stirling PDF** from **Applications** to the **Trash**. With Homebrew, run `brew uninstall --cask stirling-tools/stirling-pdf/stirling-pdf`.




- **.deb or .rpm:** remove the package with your package manager.
- **AppImage:** delete the file.
- **AUR:** `paru -R stirling-pdf-desktop`




Uninstalling keeps your data. To remove it, quit the app and delete the folders in [Data and log locations](#data-and-log-locations), and the `stirling-pdf` entries in Credential Manager or Keychain Access.

desktop/where-tools-run.title: Where your tools run
desktop/where-tools-run.description: Which desktop app tools run on your computer, which go to Stirling Cloud or your server, and what the cloud badge means.
desktop/where-tools-run.markdown:
Whether your file leaves your computer depends on your [connection mode](doc:desktop/connection-modes).

## Local Only

- Every tool runs on your computer. Nothing is uploaded.
- Tools the built-in engine can't run show a cloud badge. Running one asks you to sign in to Stirling Cloud or connect to a server.

## Stirling Cloud

- Tools run on your computer whenever the built-in engine can run them. The rest show a cloud badge and are sent to Stirling Cloud ([Files and privacy](doc:cloud/files-and-privacy)).
- Running tools by hand doesn't use credits. AI, processing folders and pipelines always use Stirling Cloud and use credits ([Plans, credits and billing](doc:cloud/plans-and-billing)).

## Self-Hosted

- Every tool runs on your server, even ones your computer could run.
- If the server can't be reached, a **Your Stirling-PDF server is unreachable** banner appears and tools the built-in engine supports run on your computer until it's back.
- Tools your server has turned off appear dimmed.

## Tools that usually need Cloud or a server

- OCR
- Converting Office documents, eBooks, HTML, web pages or email to PDF
- Converting PDF to Word, PowerPoint, RTF, HTML, Markdown, XML, PDF/A, EPUB or CBR
- **Repair**, **Detect & Split Scanned Photos** and **Replace & Invert Color**
- The **Convert images to line art** option in **Compress**

## Features that need Cloud or a server

- **AI assistant** - Stirling Cloud, or your server if its admin has set up AI ([AI assistant](doc:tools/guides/ai-assistant)).
- **Classify** - Stirling Cloud only.
- **Processing folders and pipelines** - see [Processing folders](doc:tools/workspace/processing-folders).
- **Processor** - not in the desktop app. Use it in a web browser ([Processor](doc:processor/processor)).

developers/api.title: REST API
developers/api.description: Call Stirling PDF tools over HTTP on Stirling Cloud or a self-hosted server, with API keys, examples and usage limits.
developers/api.markdown:
Every server-side tool in Stirling PDF has a REST endpoint. Send the file as `multipart/form-data` and the response is the processed file.

## Base URL, keys and reference


  

- **Base URL:** `https://api.stirling.com`
- **API key:** see [API and MCP](doc:cloud/api-and-mcp).
- **Reference:** [Stirling PDF Processing API](https://registry.scalar.com/@stirlingpdf/apis/stirling-pdf-processing-api/). To try calls in the browser, use `https://api.stirling.com/swagger-ui/index.html`.

  
  

- **Base URL:** your server's address, plus its sub-path if the admin set one ([Extra settings](doc:server/customisation/extra-settings)), for example `http://localhost:8080` or `https://example.com/pdf`.
- **API key:** sign in and open **Settings → Preferences → API Keys**. With login off, the API needs no key. Login required
- **Reference:** `/swagger-ui/index.html` on your server lists every endpoint your build has and lets you try calls. The OpenAPI spec is at `/v1/api-docs`.

  


## Authentication

Send the key on every request:

```http
X-API-KEY: your-api-key
```

The request runs as the key's owner. A missing or invalid key returns `401`.

### Global API key (self-hosted only)

An admin can set one server-wide key for scripts and automation platforms that have no user account. It is not in the shipped `settings.yml`, so set it in `custom_settings.yml` ([Extra settings](doc:server/customisation/extra-settings)) or as an environment variable:


  
    ```yaml
    security:
      customGlobalAPIKey: your-custom-api-key
    ```
  
  
    ```bash
    SECURITY_CUSTOMGLOBALAPIKEY=your-custom-api-key
    ```
  


Requests with this key run as a built-in API user. It only applies when [login is enabled](doc:server/security/sign-in-and-security).

## Endpoints

Operations live at `/api/v1/<category>/<operation>`, for example `/api/v1/misc/compress-pdf` or `/api/v1/security/add-watermark`. Look up the exact path and parameters in the reference.

- A few tools, such as the viewer and drawing a signature, run only in the browser and have no endpoint.
- Some operations exist only in the API: PDF to PostScript, EPS, PCL or XPS (`/api/v1/convert/pdf/vector`, with `outputFormat` set to `ps`, `eps`, `pcl` or `xps`), PostScript or EPS to PDF (`/api/v1/convert/vector/pdf`), decompressing a PDF's streams (`/api/v1/misc/decompress-pdf`) and the `normalize` option of `/api/v1/misc/compress-pdf`.
- File storage and sharing (`/api/v1/storage/...`) is in Swagger UI and `/v1/api-docs`, but not in the Processing API reference. On a self-hosted server it needs login ([File storage and sharing](doc:server/storage/file-storage)).
- `GET /api/v1/info/status` is a health check that needs no key. On a self-hosted server, the uptime and request-count endpoints are listed in [Usage monitoring](doc:server/operations/usage-monitoring).
- Add `?async=true` to a tool call to get a job ID back instead of the file. Poll `GET /api/v1/general/job/{jobId}`, then download the output from `GET /api/v1/general/job/{jobId}/result`.
- To run several tools in one request, use the [Pipeline API](doc:developers/pipeline-api). To let an AI assistant call the tools, use the [MCP server](doc:mcp/mcp).

## Examples

Set `STIRLING_URL` to your base URL and `STIRLING_API_KEY` to your key. The examples use bash syntax. In Windows CMD, write the variables as `%STIRLING_URL%` and `%STIRLING_API_KEY%` and end continued lines with `^` instead of `\`.

Compress a PDF:

```bash
curl -X POST "$STIRLING_URL/api/v1/misc/compress-pdf" \
  -H "X-API-KEY: $STIRLING_API_KEY" \
  -F "fileInput=@document.pdf" \
  -F "optimizeLevel=5" \
  -o compressed.pdf
```

OCR a scan in English and German. List parameters are sent as repeated fields:

```bash
curl -X POST "$STIRLING_URL/api/v1/misc/ocr-pdf" \
  -H "X-API-KEY: $STIRLING_API_KEY" \
  -F "fileInput=@scanned.pdf" \
  -F "languages=eng" \
  -F "languages=deu" \
  -F "ocrType=skip-text" \
  -F "ocrRenderType=hocr" \
  -o searchable.pdf
```

Convert a PDF to Word:

```bash
curl -X POST "$STIRLING_URL/api/v1/convert/pdf/word" \
  -H "X-API-KEY: $STIRLING_API_KEY" \
  -F "fileInput=@document.pdf" \
  -F "outputFormat=docx" \
  -o document.docx
```

## Automation platforms

There are no dedicated plugins for n8n, Zapier, Make or Power Automate. Use the platform's generic HTTP request action: method `POST`, body `multipart/form-data`, the file in `fileInput`, and the key in an `X-API-KEY` header. To chain steps in one call, send a pipeline to the [Pipeline API](doc:developers/pipeline-api).

## Usage allowance

Running regular tools yourself in the app doesn't count. Tool calls made with an API key do:

- **Stirling Cloud:** every API-key call uses your team's credits. When the free credits or your spend cap run out, calls return `402` with `PAYG_LIMIT_REACHED`. See [Plans, credits and billing](doc:cloud/plans-and-billing).
- **Self-hosted:** calls use the server's processing allowance, and return `402` with `ACCOUNT_LINK_REQUIRED` when it runs out. See [Processing allowance](doc:server/licensing/connect-to-stirling-cloud).

developers/contributing.title: Contributing
developers/contributing.description: Set up a Stirling PDF development environment, run it locally and submit changes, translations and docs.
developers/contributing.markdown:
Stirling PDF is open-core and lives on [GitHub](https://github.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-PDF). Read the repository's [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-PDF/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) first. In particular, comment on (or open) an issue and wait to be assigned before you start work.

## Prerequisites

- Git and Docker
- Java JDK 25 (Gradle is included in the repository)
- Node.js 22 or later, with npm
- [Task](https://taskfile.dev/installation/), the project's command runner
- [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), for the Python AI engine
- Rust and Cargo, only for the desktop app

## Set up and run

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-PDF.git
cd Stirling-PDF
task install
task dev
```

`task install` installs the frontend and AI engine dependencies. Gradle fetches the backend's own. `task dev` starts the backend and frontend together on free ports, 8080 and 5173 when they are available, and opens the browser. To start the AI engine as well, run `task dev:all`.

To run parts on their own, use separate terminals:

| Command | Starts |
|---|---|
| `task backend:dev` | Backend on `http://localhost:8080` |
| `task frontend:dev` | Frontend on `http://localhost:5173` |
| `task engine:dev` | AI engine on `http://localhost:5001` |
| `task desktop:dev` | Desktop app |

With the backend running, the API reference is at `http://localhost:8080/swagger-ui/index.html`. Run `task --list` for every command.

The LibreOffice, Tesseract, qpdf and WeasyPrint features need those programs installed locally. Without them, the matching tools are turned off.

If you run the frontend dev server behind a reverse proxy or a custom hostname, list the allowed hostnames in `FRONTEND_ALLOWED_HOSTS`, for example `FRONTEND_ALLOWED_HOSTS=dev.example.com,localhost`.

## Before you open a pull request

```bash
task fix
task check
```

`task fix` formats and auto-fixes the code, and `task check` must pass. Keep one change per pull request and use the PR template.

## Build

| Command | Builds |
|---|---|
| `task build` | Backend and frontend |
| `./gradlew clean build -PbuildWithFrontend=true` | One JAR with the frontend bundled in |
| `task docker:build` | The standard Docker image (`docker:build:fat` and `docker:build:ultra-lite` for the others) |
| `task desktop:build` | Desktop app installers |

## Adding a tool

1. Add the backend endpoint ([Adding a new feature to the backend](https://github.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-PDF/blob/main/DeveloperGuide.md#adding-a-new-feature-to-the-backend-api) in the Developer Guide).
2. Add the frontend tool ([ADDING_TOOLS.md](https://github.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-PDF/blob/main/ADDING_TOOLS.md)).
3. Add the tool's text to the `en-US` `translation.toml` only. Other languages are handled separately.

The [Developer Guide](https://github.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-PDF/blob/main/DeveloperGuide.md) covers the architecture, and the [devGuide folder](https://github.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-PDF/tree/main/devGuide) has guides on error handling, comments and more.

## Translations

Each language has one file at `frontend/editor/public/locales/<language>/translation.toml`. `en-US` is the source: add new text there first. For counts, use i18next plural suffixes on the key, such as `_one` and `_other`. To add or translate a language, see [How to add new languages](https://github.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-PDF/blob/main/devGuide/HowToAddNewLanguage.md).

## Documentation

These docs live in the [Stirling-Tools.github.io](https://github.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-Tools.github.io) repository. Open a pull request there with your change.

developers/pipeline-api.title: Pipeline API
developers/pipeline-api.description: Run several Stirling PDF tools on one or more files in a single request with a JSON pipeline and POST /api/v1/pipeline/handleData.
developers/pipeline-api.markdown:
Send files and a JSON pipeline to `POST /api/v1/pipeline/handleData` to run several tools in one request. The same JSON format is used by server [folder scanning](doc:server/storage/folder-scanning).

Authentication and base URLs are the same as for the [REST API](doc:developers/api). Pipeline steps count as automation; see [Processing allowance](doc:server/licensing/connect-to-stirling-cloud).

## JSON format

```json
{
  "name": "Split then compress",
  "pipeline": [
    {
      "operation": "/api/v1/general/split-pages",
      "parameters": { "pageNumbers": "5" }
    },
    {
      "operation": "/api/v1/misc/compress-pdf",
      "parameters": { "optimizeLevel": 5 }
    }
  ]
}
```

- `operation` is the full endpoint path: `/api/v1/misc/compress-pdf`, not `compress-pdf`.
- `parameters` uses the endpoint's own field names. Leave out `fileInput`, as each file is passed in for you. Exported files contain `"fileInput": "automated"`, which is ignored.
- A list such as `"languages": ["eng", "deu"]` is sent as repeated form fields.
- Steps run in order, and the same operation can appear more than once with different parameters.
- Other top-level fields (`description`, `icon`, `_examples`) are ignored. `outputDir` and `outputFileName` only apply to folder scanning.

## Start from an Automate export

Build the workflow in [Automate](doc:tools/guides/automate) and click **Export for Folder Scanning**, not **Export**. This downloads `<name>.folder-scan.json` with each step's endpoint path filled in. Before you use it, rename each step's parameters to the endpoint's field names, for example `compressionLevel` to `optimizeLevel` for Compress, as endpoints ignore names they don't know.

## Operations

A step can call any tool endpoint under `/api/v1/general/`, `/misc/`, `/security/`, `/convert/`, `/filter/`, `/integration/`, `/docparse/` or `/ai/tools/`. Find paths and parameters in the [API reference](doc:developers/api).

- Operations that need a second file, such as an image watermark or an overlay PDF, can't be used in a pipeline. Call those endpoints directly.
- Multi-file operations such as `/api/v1/general/merge-pdfs` get every file in one call.
- A file of a type a step can't take is dropped from the run, and the server logs it.
- `/api/v1/integration/external-api-call` sends the file to a saved **Custom API** connection, passed by its ID as `connectionId`. Only self-hosted admins can create these ([Integrations](doc:processor/integrations)).
- AI steps (`/api/v1/ai/tools/...`) need [AI set up](doc:server/ai/ai) on a self-hosted server.

## Filters

A filter step keeps a file only when its condition is true. Files that don't match leave the pipeline without an error.

| Operation | Keeps the file when |
|---|---|
| `/api/v1/filter/filter-contains-text` | it contains `text` (limit the check with `pageNumbers`) |
| `/api/v1/filter/filter-contains-image` | it contains an image (limit the check with `pageNumbers`) |
| `/api/v1/filter/filter-page-count` | the page count compares to `pageCount` |
| `/api/v1/filter/filter-page-size` | the first page compares to `standardPageSize` (A0 to A6, LETTER, LEGAL) |
| `/api/v1/filter/filter-file-size` | the file size in bytes compares to `fileSize` |
| `/api/v1/filter/filter-page-rotation` | the first page's rotation compares to `rotation` |

The last four take a `comparator` of `Greater`, `Equal` or `Less`.

This pipeline OCRs only PDFs that contain an image. `skip-text` leaves pages that already have text alone:

```json
{
  "name": "OCR PDFs containing images",
  "pipeline": [
    {"operation": "/api/v1/filter/filter-contains-image", "parameters": {"pageNumbers": "all"}},
    {"operation": "/api/v1/misc/ocr-pdf", "parameters": {"languages": ["eng"], "ocrType": "skip-text"}}
  ]
}
```

## Run a pipeline

`POST /api/v1/pipeline/handleData` with `multipart/form-data`:

| Field | Required | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `fileInput` | Yes | One or more files. Repeat the field for each file. |
| `json` | Yes | The pipeline JSON as a string. |

```bash
curl -X POST "$STIRLING_URL/api/v1/pipeline/handleData" \
  -H "X-API-KEY: $STIRLING_API_KEY" \
  -F "fileInput=@input.pdf" \
  -F 'json={
    "name": "Repair then compress",
    "pipeline": [
      {"operation": "/api/v1/misc/repair", "parameters": {}},
      {"operation": "/api/v1/misc/compress-pdf", "parameters": {"optimizeLevel": 2}}
    ]
  }' \
  -o result.pdf
```

- One output file comes back as the file itself. Several come back as `output.zip`.
- Add `?async=true` to get a job ID instead. Poll `GET /api/v1/general/job/{jobId}` and download from `GET /api/v1/general/job/{jobId}/result`.

developers/technologies.title: Open-source components
developers/technologies.description: The main open-source libraries and programs Stirling PDF is built on.
developers/technologies.markdown:
Stirling PDF is built on these open-source projects. The full source is on [GitHub](https://github.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-PDF).

## Server

- **[PDFBox](https://pdfbox.apache.org/)** - core PDF reading and editing
- **JPDFium** - PDFium-based engine for merge, split and reading text and tables
- **[Tabula](https://github.com/tabulapdf/tabula-java)** - table extraction
- **[LibreOffice](https://www.libreoffice.org/)** - office document conversion
- **[qpdf](https://qpdf.sourceforge.io/)** and **[Ghostscript](https://www.ghostscript.com/)** - PDF optimisation and compression
- **[OCRmyPDF](https://ocrmypdf.readthedocs.io/)** with **[Tesseract](https://github.com/tesseract-ocr/tesseract)** - text recognition
- **[Calibre](https://calibre-ebook.com/)** - e-book conversion
- **[ImageMagick](https://imagemagick.org/)** and **[OpenCV](https://opencv.org/)** - image processing
- **[WeasyPrint](https://weasyprint.org/)** - HTML to PDF

## AI engine

- **[FastAPI](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/)** and **[Pydantic AI](https://ai.pydantic.dev/)** (Python)

## Web app

- **[React](https://react.dev/)** and **[TypeScript](https://www.typescriptlang.org/)**, built with **[Vite](https://vitejs.dev/)**
- **[EmbedPDF](https://www.embedpdf.com/)** and **[PDF.js](https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/)** - viewing and annotation
- **[pdf-lib](https://github.com/cantoo-scribe/pdf-lib)** (Cantoo fork) - PDF editing in the browser
- **[Mantine](https://mantine.dev/)** - UI components
- **[i18next](https://www.i18next.com/)** - translations for 40+ languages

## Desktop app

- **[Tauri](https://tauri.app/)** - native app for Windows, macOS and Linux

mcp/mcp.markdown:
Stirling PDF has a built-in [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) (MCP) server. Connect an AI assistant such as Claude, Codex or VS Code, and it can convert, edit, secure and process documents with your Stirling PDF tools. Every action runs as your account.

| Where Stirling PDF runs | MCP endpoint | Sign-in |
|---|---|---|
| Stirling Cloud | `https://api.stirling.com/mcp` | Your Stirling account. No key to copy. |
| Self-hosted server | `https://your-server/mcp` | OAuth or API key, set by your admin. Off by default. |

The tools the server exposes, their arguments and results.


For admins: turn MCP on and choose how clients sign in.



To call Stirling PDF from your own code instead, see the [REST API](doc:developers/api).

mcp/tools.title: MCP tools reference
mcp/tools.description: The tools the Stirling PDF MCP server exposes, how to call them and what they return.
mcp/tools.markdown:
## Tools

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `stirling_describe_operation` | Returns the parameters and JSON schema for one operation. |
| `stirling_pages` | Page operations: merge, split, rotate, rearrange, crop, delete, overlay, add blank pages. |
| `stirling_convert` | Conversions to and from PDF (Word, images, HTML and more). |
| `stirling_misc` | Compress, OCR, stamp, watermark, metadata, flatten, repair and similar. |
| `stirling_security` | Passwords, redaction, sanitising, certificate signing and signature validation. |
| `stirling_upload` | Stores a file on the server and returns a `fileId`, so several operations can reuse it. |
| `stirling_download` | Returns a stored file by `fileId`, as base64, up to the inline limit. |
| `stirling_ai` | Runs AI capabilities. Needs AI to be set up. |

Operation IDs are the short endpoint names, such as `compress-pdf`. Each tool lists the operations it has, and an admin can hide some. Filters and the [Pipeline API](doc:developers/pipeline-api) aren't available over MCP.

## Calling a tool

Call `stirling_describe_operation` with an `operation` first to get its parameters. Then call the category tool:

| Argument | Required | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `operation` | Yes | The operation ID, for example `compress-pdf`. |
| `parameters` | No | An object of the operation's parameters. |
| `file` | No | The input document as base64. The usual way to send a file. |
| `fileName` | No | The original file name with its extension. |
| `fileId` | No | A file stored with `stirling_upload`, or an earlier result, instead of `file`. |

```json
{"name": "stirling_misc", "arguments": {"operation": "compress-pdf", "fileName": "report.pdf", "file": "<base64>", "parameters": {"optimizeLevel": 5}}}
```

Results:

- A JSON result comes back as text.
- A file result comes back inline as base64 (`stirling://file/{fileId}`) with its `fileId`, up to the server's inline limit (10 MB by default on self-hosted servers).
- A larger result returns only a `fileId`, which you can pass to the next operation. `stirling_download` has the same limit, so it can't return that file either. On a self-hosted server an admin can raise the limit ([MCP server settings](doc:server/automation/mcp-server)).

## AI capabilities

`stirling_ai` takes an `operation` (a capability ID), a `parameters` object and, for capabilities that read a document, a `fileId`. The capabilities are `pdf-question-answer`, `pdf-edit-plan`, `pdf-comment-generate`, `agent-draft`, `agent-revise`, `agent-next-action`, `math-audit-examine` and `math-audit-deliberate`. Use `stirling_describe_operation` to get each one's schema.

AI is on for Stirling Cloud. On a self-hosted server an admin must set it up ([AI on your server](doc:server/ai/ai)).

processor/documents.title: Documents
processor/documents.markdown:
Open **Processor → Documents** to confirm a pipeline ran on a file, see which operation handled it and when, and spot anything that failed. Each row shows a file name, the operation, who ran it, the outcome and the time.

![Documents table with filters and CSV export](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-Tools.github.io/main/static/img/processor/documents.png)

## Find and inspect activity

Search by filename or ID and use the status filters to narrow the list. Click a row to open its **Overview** and **Audit** details.

The page displays up to **40** recent file-operation records. A file processed several times can appear more than once. Reload the page to refresh the list.

**Export CSV** downloads all loaded rows, including any hidden by the current filters. For failed runs and error details, open [Review](doc:processor/review).

## What you see

Documents shows processing records, not the files themselves: files cannot be opened or downloaded from here. On Stirling Cloud you see your team's records. On a self-hosted server you see records for the whole server.

On a self-hosted server, records are kept for up to 30 days without an Enterprise licence. For retention settings and full audit searches, see [Audit logging](doc:server/security/audit-logging).

processor/getting-started.title: Create your first pipeline
processor/getting-started.markdown:
Build, test and switch on a pipeline that compresses PDFs. You need [management access](doc:processor/setup-and-access).

The editor walkthrough works on Stirling Cloud and self-hosted servers. The folder walkthrough needs a self-hosted server, because Stirling Cloud has no Folder sources.

## Compress editor downloads

1. Open **Processor → Pipelines → New custom pipeline** and name it **Compress downloads**.
2. Choose **Editor** as the input and set **Runs on** to **Every export**.
3. Select **Add a tool**, add **Compress** and choose the settings. Leave the destination as **Editor**.
4. Select **Test with a file** and check the result.
5. Select **Create pipeline**.
6. Open a PDF in the editor and download it. The download is the compressed file.

An editor pipeline runs for everyone in your team, and each run uses credits ([Credits](doc:processor/setup-and-access)). To read from or deliver to storage instead, connect an [Amazon S3 source](doc:processor/sources).

## Compress files from a server folder

An administrator must first allow the folders you use ([Processor server settings](doc:server/automation/processor-settings)).

### 1. Connect an inbox

1. Open **Processor → Sources → Connect source**.
2. Choose **Folder**.
3. Name it **Invoice inbox** and under **Folder** enter a path on the server, such as `/data/processor/inbox`.
4. Leave **Folder depth** at **Top level only**.
5. Expand **Advanced**. Under **After processing**, choose **Keep it, and only process it again if it changes** so testing does not delete originals.
6. Select **Create source**.

![Folder source configuration with advanced processing controls](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-Tools.github.io/main/static/img/processor/folder-source.png)

Originals stay in place, and an unchanged file is not processed again.

### 2. Connect an output folder

Create another Folder source named **Processed invoices**, with a path such as `/data/processor/processed`. Keep it outside the inbox so the pipeline does not process its own output.

### 3. Build the pipeline

1. Open **Pipelines → New custom pipeline**.
2. Name it **Compress incoming invoices**.
3. Choose **Invoice inbox** as the input and leave the trigger at **Manual only**.
4. Select **Add a tool**, add **Compress** and choose the compression settings.
5. Select **Processed invoices** as the destination.
6. Complete any settings the builder highlights.

![Compress incoming invoices pipeline: Invoice inbox, Compress, and Processed invoices](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-Tools.github.io/main/static/img/processor/first-pipeline.png)

### 4. Test one document

Select **Test with a file** and choose a sample PDF. The results come back as a download and are not delivered to the destination. Check the content, page count and file size.

![Test with a file button above the pipeline steps](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-Tools.github.io/main/static/img/processor/test-with-a-file.png)

### 5. Save, then turn it on

Save with **Create paused** while you finish checking. When you are ready, open the pipeline, change its trigger to **Folder watch**, select **Save changes**, then select **Activate**.

Place a new PDF in the inbox and confirm the result reaches the output folder.

### 6. Check it runs

Open [Documents](doc:processor/documents) for the processing record and [Review](doc:processor/review) if a run fails. Before switching the inbox to **Delete the file**, confirm deliveries work: originals are removed once delivered ([Decide what happens to originals](doc:processor/sources)).

processor/integrations.title: Integrations
processor/integrations.markdown:
Save a connection once under **Processor → Integrations**, then use it in sources and pipelines.

![Storage integrations with connected and available services](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-Tools.github.io/main/static/img/processor/integrations.png)

## Connect a service

1. Open **Processor → Integrations**, find the service, and select **Connect**.
2. Give the connection a name and enter its address and credentials.
3. Select **Save connection**. The **Works with** column then shows where you can use it.

On a self-hosted server, only administrators and team owners can connect services, and Custom API needs an administrator.

## Use an integration in a pipeline

In the [pipeline builder](doc:processor/pipelines), select **Add a tool** and look under **Send to another system**. Pick what you want to happen, such as **Scan for viruses** or **Post a message to Slack**, choose your saved connection under **Account** and fill in the step's fields. The step runs at that point in the pipeline, like any other tool.

Storage services work differently: choose them when you [connect a source](doc:processor/sources), to read documents from them or deliver results to them.

Security steps can stop a run: if a scan finds a problem, the document is held back and appears in [Review](doc:processor/review). Notification, email, and audit steps leave the document unchanged.

## Available integrations

| Integration | Type | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| **S3 storage** (Amazon S3 or S3-compatible) | Storage | Input and destination for [sources](doc:processor/sources) |
| **SFTP** | Storage | Input for sources |
| **FTP / FTPS** | Storage | Input for sources |
| **SMB / Network share** | Storage | Input for sources |
| **Vector database** (Weaviate, Pinecone) | Storage | Destination for [Ingestion](doc:processor/policies/ingestion) chunks |
| **Nextcloud** | Storage | Upload the processed document to a folder |
| **Jira** | Storage | Attach the processed document to an issue |
| **Confluence** | Storage | Attach the processed document to a page |
| **Cloudmersive** | Security | Scan for viruses; the run stops if the file is not clean |
| **Cloudmersive Advanced Scan** | Security | Block documents that contain macros, executables, scripts, or embedded objects |
| **ClamAV (self-hosted)** | Security | Scan for viruses on your own server, so nothing leaves your network |
| **Presidio (self-hosted)** | Security | Detect personal data in the text you give it, on your own server |
| **Splunk** | Audit | Send an audit event for each document |
| **Elasticsearch** | Audit | Index an audit event for each document |
| **Sumo Logic** | Audit | Send an audit event to an HTTP collector |
| **SendGrid** | Notify | Email the processed document as an attachment |
| **Mailgun** | Notify | Email the processed document as an attachment |
| **Slack** | Notify | Post a message to a channel |
| **Microsoft Teams** | Notify | Post a message to a channel |
| **Discord** | Notify | Post a message to a channel |
| **Google Chat** | Notify | Post a message to a space |
| **Zapier & Make** | Notify | Trigger a Zap or Make scenario |
| **n8n** | Notify | Tell a workflow, send it the document, let it process the document, or ask it to approve the run |
| **Webhook** | Notify | Post the document, or just its details, to a URL you choose |
| **Custom API** | Advanced | Call any HTTP API; see [Custom API](#custom-api) |

Messages and audit events can include details from the document and the run, such as `{{document.filename}}` and `{{run.policyName}}`. See [Placeholders](#placeholders).

## Custom API

Use **Custom API** to call a service that has no ready-made integration, such as an internal records system or a review queue.

1. Create a **Custom API** connection with the service's **Base URL** and **Authentication**: a bearer token, a username and password, a token in a custom header, logging in for a token, or none.
2. In the pipeline builder, select **Add a tool → Send to another system → Call a custom API**, and choose the connection under **Account**.
3. Enter the **Path** and **Method**. The path is added to the connection's base URL and can never reach another host.
4. Choose **How to send the document**: as a file upload (multipart), inside a JSON payload, or as raw file bytes.
5. Choose **What to do with the reply**: keep the document and record the reply, or replace the document with what comes back.

For example, a JSON body that sends the file with its name:

```json
{
  "name": "{{document.filename}}",
  "content": "{{document.base64}}"
}
```

Custom API is not available on Stirling Cloud. Test runs also call the service, so point new pipelines at a test environment first.

### Placeholders

Paths, headers, messages, and JSON bodies can include these values, filled in for each document:

| Placeholder | Value |
|---|---|
| `{{document.filename}}`, `{{document.extension}}` | File name and extension |
| `{{document.sizeBytes}}`, `{{document.pageCount}}` | File size in bytes and page count |
| `{{document.title}}`, `{{document.author}}` | PDF title and author |
| `{{document.sha256}}` | SHA-256 hash of the file |
| `{{document.base64}}` | The file itself, for JSON bodies |
| `{{run.policyName}}`, `{{run.runId}}`, `{{run.timestamp}}` | Pipeline name, run ID, and time of the run |

## Storage connection settings

| Connection | Required settings | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| **S3 storage** | Bucket, region, access key ID, secret access key; an endpoint only for S3-compatible storage | S3 inputs and destinations |
| **SFTP** | Host, port, username, password or private key; optional passphrase and host-key fingerprint | SFTP input |
| **FTP / FTPS** | Host, port, username, password, encryption and connection mode | FTP input |
| **SMB / Network share** | Host, share, credentials, and any required domain | Network-drive input |

## Server settings

Connection secrets are encrypted at rest. On a self-hosted server, the encryption key and connections to internal addresses are administrator settings; see [Processor server settings](doc:server/automation/processor-settings).

processor/pipelines.title: Pipelines
processor/pipelines.markdown:
A pipeline is a saved workflow: where documents come from, the steps to run and where the results go. Open **Processor → Pipelines** to manage your pipelines and policies.

![Pipelines list and template gallery](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-Tools.github.io/main/static/img/processor/pipelines.png)

## Create a workflow

Choose **New custom pipeline** to build one yourself, or select **Set up** on one of the [policies](doc:processor/policies/policies) for a guided form.

![Pipeline builder with input, operation chain, and settings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-Tools.github.io/main/static/img/processor/pipeline-builder.png)

1. Name the pipeline and select an input source.
2. Choose when it runs.
3. Add tools in the order they should run and configure each step.
4. Choose a destination, or return the modified document to the editor.
5. Test the steps, then select **Create pipeline** or **Create paused**.

For a step-by-step example, see [Create your first pipeline](doc:processor/getting-started).

## Inputs and triggers

| Input | Triggers |
|---|---|
| **Editor** | **Every upload** or **Every export**; see [Editor](doc:processor/sources) |
| **Folder** | **Manual only**, **Scheduled** or **Folder watch** |
| **Amazon S3**, **SFTP**, **FTP**, **Network drive** | **Manual only** or **Scheduled** |
| **Webhook** | **webhook** (runs as each signed delivery arrives), **Manual only** or **Scheduled**; see [Webhooks](doc:processor/sources) |

## Steps and supporting files

Each tool must accept the previous step's output format. A tool can appear more than once, with separate settings for each step.

Integration steps are under **Add a tool → Send to another system** ([Integrations](doc:processor/integrations)). A **Classify** step uses AI to label documents for [routing](doc:processor/policies/routing); see [Classification](doc:processor/policies/classification).

Upload supporting files, such as stamp images or signing certificates, in the step settings. They are saved for future runs and shared within the team. Files must be non-empty and no larger than **50 MB**. Referenced files cannot be deleted until removed from the pipeline.

## Enforce as policy

A pipeline with the **Editor** as its input runs automatically for everyone in the team when they upload or export a file. **Enforce as policy** decides what happens when it fails:

| When it fails | Ordinary pipeline | Enforced as policy |
|---|---|---|
| On upload | The file stays as it was uploaded, and the failure is reported. | The file is blocked. The person can retry or close it. |
| On export | The file is downloaded unprocessed, with a warning. | The download is cancelled. |

Use it when a rule must hold for every document, such as redacting personal data before anything leaves the editor, or converting to PDF/A before archiving.

Turn on **Enforce as policy** at the top of the pipeline builder; for defaults in setup forms, see [Policies](doc:processor/policies/policies). Enforced pipelines show as **Policy** in the pipelines list. Only people who can manage pipelines can change it.

## Test and inspect output

**Test with a file** runs the current steps, including unsaved edits, and returns outputs for download. It does not write to the configured storage destination. External integration calls still run.

After checking the output, run one controlled live input to confirm delivery to storage.

## Save, pause, and edit

Open a pipeline to edit it, then select **Save changes**.

**Pause** stops future automatic runs and **Activate** resumes them. Both take effect immediately and do not save pending step changes.

## Destinations

Folder and S3 destinations save processed files, using a new filename when one already exists. Vector database destinations receive prepared chunks from an [Ingestion](doc:processor/policies/ingestion) pipeline.

Editor pipelines can return the modified document to the editor. With [routing](doc:processor/policies/routing), the fallback destination receives unmatched files.

processor/policies/classification.title: Classification
processor/policies/classification.markdown:
The Classification policy uses AI to work out what each document is, such as an invoice, contract or resume, and tags its metadata with the matching types. Tagged documents are easier to file and search, and [Routing](doc:processor/policies/routing) can send each type to its own destination.

On a self-hosted server, Classification needs an administrator to set up AI with **Document classification** turned on ([AI on your server](doc:server/ai/ai)).

## Set up Classification

1. Open **Processor → Pipelines** and select **Set up** on **Classification**.
2. Review the **Classification labels**. They are a built-in set of document types, shared across your whole team.
3. Choose the documents to process. For editor files, Classification runs on **Every upload** by default.
4. Select **Create pipeline**.

A document can receive several labels when more than one type fits.

## Classify inside other pipelines

Add a **Classify** step to any pipeline in the [pipeline builder](doc:processor/pipelines). Put it before delivery when you want to route documents by type. To route without AI, match on file properties instead; see [Routing](doc:processor/policies/routing).

processor/policies/compliance.title: Compliance
processor/policies/compliance.markdown:
The Compliance policy prepares documents for long-term archiving. It strips hidden data, converts each document to PDF/A, and checks the result meets the standard before it is delivered. By default it runs when people export files from the editor.

![Compliance policy setup form with PDF/A conversion and validation settings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-Tools.github.io/main/static/img/processor/compliance-template.png)

## Set up Compliance

1. Open **Processor → Pipelines** and select **Set up** on **Compliance**.
2. Keep the actions you need:
   - **Strip active content** removes scripts, attachments, and document metadata. Fonts are kept, because PDF/A requires them.
   - **Convert to PDF/A for archiving** rewrites the document in the archival format. Choose the **Archival profile**: PDF/A-2b suits most archives, PDF/A-1b is the strictest and most widely accepted, and PDF/A-3b also allows attachments.
   - **Check the document meets the standard** validates the finished file and stops the run if it does not pass.
3. Choose the documents to process and where results go.
4. Select **Create pipeline**.

[Enforce as policy](doc:processor/pipelines) is on by default, so files that fail the check cannot leave the editor.

## Before you roll it out

PDF/A conversion invalidates existing digital signatures. Convert before signing, or keep signed originals separately.

Conversion and validation failures appear in [Review](doc:processor/review) with the reason, so you can fix the source document and try again.

processor/policies/ingestion.title: Ingestion
processor/policies/ingestion.markdown:
The Ingestion policy prepares documents for knowledge search. Open **Processor → Pipelines**, find **Ingestion** under **Templates**, and select **Set up**.

The default chain runs OCR, then prepares searchable chunks with the AI engine. On a self-hosted server, an administrator must [run the AI engine](doc:server/ai/run-the-ai-engine); chunking does not work through Stirling Cloud AI.

## Configure processing

1. Review **Make text searchable**. The preset uses English OCR; use **Customise** to change the OCR step's languages when needed.
2. Leave **Prepare for knowledge search** on to prepare chunks. Turn it off if you only need OCR.
3. Under **Documents to process**, choose **Files opened in the editor** or a saved input source. Use **Connect input source** if the location is not set up yet.
4. Choose when the input runs. Editor input runs on upload or export; other inputs offer the triggers their source type supports.
5. Choose the output type and destination described below.
6. Resolve any readiness messages, then select **Create pipeline**.

![Ingestion setup with processing and input settings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-Tools.github.io/main/static/img/processor/ingestion-setup.png)

## Choose the output

![Ingestion output menu with knowledge base, connected database, and export choices](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-Tools.github.io/main/static/img/processor/ingestion-output.png)

| Output type | Result | Requirements |
|---|---|---|
| **Stirling knowledge base** | Indexes searchable chunks in Stirling and returns the processed PDF to the selected destination. | Reachable AI engine and a configured embedding provider. |
| **Connected vector database** | Sends chunks to the selected database, which generates embeddings; returns an indexing receipt. | Reachable AI engine and an enabled [vector database source](doc:processor/sources) with its connection and collection. |
| **Export chunks without a database** | Saves the processed PDF and JSONL chunks to the selected destination. | Reachable AI engine; no database or embedding provider needed. |

Select an enabled destination for server inputs and exports. For Editor input, choose **Return results to editor** or **Keep originals and send to a destination**.

## Adjust chunk settings

Expand **Chunk settings** to change how extracted text is divided for retrieval:

| Setting | Default | Accepted values |
|---|---|---|
| **Chunk size** | `512` | Whole number from `64` to `32768` characters |
| **Overlap** | `64` | Whole number from `0` to `4096`, smaller than the chunk size |

Start with the defaults and check retrieval against your documents before changing them. Changing chunk settings does not rebuild documents already stored in a knowledge base.

## Check readiness and originals

Resolve any readiness messages and select **Check again**. On a self-hosted server, an administrator can open the engine settings from **Open AI settings**.

Choose what happens to originals with the source's [After processing](doc:processor/sources) setting. When a [processing folder](doc:tools/workspace/processing-folders) delivers to a vector database, originals are kept.

Test a document, inspect the resulting PDF or export, and try a search in the knowledge base before switching on ongoing ingestion. Use [Review](doc:processor/review) to investigate failures.

processor/policies/policies.title: Policies
processor/policies/policies.markdown:
Policies are ready-made pipelines with a simple setup form: [Ingestion](doc:processor/policies/ingestion), [Security](doc:processor/policies/security), [Classification](doc:processor/policies/classification), [Compliance](doc:processor/policies/compliance) and [Routing](doc:processor/policies/routing).

Every policy you set up is saved as an ordinary [pipeline](doc:processor/pipelines). It leaves **Templates**, appears under **All pipelines** and runs the same way.

## Set up a policy

1. Open **Processor → Pipelines**.
2. Under **Templates**, select **Set up** on the policy you want.
3. Turn on the actions you need. Expand an action to change its settings.
4. Choose the documents to process, when to run, and where results go.
5. Select **Create pipeline**.

For more control, select **Customise** to open the same pipeline in the full [pipeline builder](doc:processor/pipelines), keeping everything set so far. Once the pipeline goes beyond what the form supports, it opens in the builder from then on.

When documents come from the editor, [Enforce as policy](doc:processor/pipelines) is on by default for every policy except Classification, so files that fail are blocked. Turn it off in the setup form to let them through with a warning.

processor/policies/routing.title: Routing
processor/policies/routing.markdown:
Routing sends each processed document to the destination that matches it, with a fallback for anything else. Set it up with the Routing policy, or in any pipeline's destination settings.

## Set up the Routing policy

1. Open **Processor → Pipelines** and select **Set up** on **Routing**.
2. Under **Watch**, choose the folder, bucket or webhook the policy watches, or connect a new [source](doc:processor/sources).
3. Select **Add a route** for each group of documents, choose what to match and choose its destination.
4. Under **Everything else goes to**, choose the fallback destination.
5. Select **Create pipeline**.

A watched folder runs as files arrive and a webhook as deliveries come in; other sources are checked every hour. Routes that match on document type add a Classify step, which needs AI classification ([Classification](doc:processor/policies/classification)). Routes on file properties work without AI.

## Matching options

| Match by | Values |
|---|---|
| **File extension** | `pdf`, `docx`, `png`, and other extensions |
| **Exact filename** | Complete filename |
| **PDF title** | Title metadata |
| **PDF author** | Author metadata |
| **Document type (AI classification)** | Labels produced by a Classify step |

Enter exact property values separated by commas. Wildcards and regular expressions are not supported.

## Add rules in the pipeline builder

1. Create writable [sources](doc:processor/sources) for your destinations.
2. In the pipeline's destination settings, turn on **Send document types to different places**.
3. For each rule, select **Add a route**, choose **Match by**, enter the values and choose a destination.
4. Rules are checked in the order you add them, and the first match wins.
5. Under **Everything else goes to**, choose a fallback destination for unmatched files.

For classification-based routing, include a **Classify** step before delivery.

## Example without AI

| Order | Condition | Destination |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | File extension is `pdf` | PDF archive |
| 2 | File extension is `png, jpg, jpeg` | Image archive |
| Fallback | No rule matches | Unsorted |

Test both matching and unmatched files. If an earlier step converts the document, check that your rules match the output format.

processor/policies/security.title: Security
processor/policies/security.markdown:
The Security policy protects documents before they are shared. It redacts personal data, removes JavaScript, and can add a watermark. By default it runs when people export files from the editor.

## Set up Security

1. Open **Processor → Pipelines** and select **Set up** on **Security**.
2. Keep the actions you need:
   - **Redact sensitive information** finds US Social Security numbers and payment card numbers by default. Expand it to change what it looks for.
   - **Strip active content** removes JavaScript so nothing runs when the document is opened.
   - **Apply a watermark** starts switched off. Turn it on and enter the text, such as "Confidential".
3. Choose the documents to process. For editor files, Security runs on **Every export** by default, so files are protected as they leave the editor.
4. Select **Create pipeline**.

[Enforce as policy](doc:processor/pipelines) is on by default, so a file the policy cannot protect is not exported.

## Check the results

Redaction and the watermark turn pages into images by default, so redacted text cannot be recovered and the watermark cannot be removed. The processed file has no selectable or searchable text.

Test with a sample document and check the output, including searching and copying text, before rolling the policy out to your team.

processor/processor.title: Stirling Processor
processor/processor.markdown:
Stirling Processor runs PDF workflows for you, in bulk or as new files arrive: **source → steps → destination**.

![Processor home: documents from five sources flowing through five policies, with 8,788 delivered and 272 failed in 24 hours](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-Tools.github.io/main/static/img/processor/processor-home.gif)

Not in the desktop app; see [Setup and access](doc:processor/setup-and-access).

## Start here

Follow [Create your first pipeline](doc:processor/getting-started) to build, test and switch on a compression pipeline.

## Find your way around

| Page | Use it to |
|---|---|
| [Sources](doc:processor/sources) | Connect folders, storage services and webhooks. |
| [Pipelines](doc:processor/pipelines) | Build, test, pause and edit workflows. |
| [Policies](doc:processor/policies/policies) | Set up ready-made pipelines: Ingestion, Security, Classification, Compliance and Routing. |
| [Documents](doc:processor/documents) | View recent processing activity and export it as CSV. |
| [Review](doc:processor/review) | Investigate and resolve failed runs. |
| [Integrations](doc:processor/integrations) | Save connections to external services. |

[Processing folders](doc:tools/workspace/processing-folders) attach a workflow to a folder in your file library.

processor/review.title: Review
processor/review.description: Find out why processing failed, fix the cause, and retry.
processor/review.markdown:
Open **Processor → Review** to see why a pipeline run or editor operation failed, correct the cause, and try again.

![Review queue with issue details and available actions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-Tools.github.io/main/static/img/processor/review.png)

## Investigate an issue

1. Start with **Open** issues.
2. Search by issue, user or error, or filter by **Type**, **Source**, **User** and **Raised in**.
3. Choose **View error** from the row menu. Use **Copy error** to copy the diagnostic.
4. Fix the cause, then use the recovery action offered or rerun the pipeline.

Repeated issues can be grouped with an occurrence count. The date shows the latest occurrence.

**Dismiss** closes an issue without rerunning it. Switch to **Closed** to see resolved issues and their outcomes.

You see issues from your own runs. People who manage pipelines also see issues from the team's runs, including scheduled and folder-watch runs that have no user to tell; see [Who can open and manage it](doc:processor/setup-and-access).

The page loads up to **50** recent records and refreshes every **30 seconds** while visible. Search and filters apply to those records.

processor/setup-and-access.title: Setup and access
processor/setup-and-access.markdown:
Login required

## Open Processor

Open Stirling PDF in a web browser and select **Processor** in the left bar. On Stirling Cloud you can also go straight to [stirling.com/app/processor](https://stirling.com/app/processor). Processor is not part of the desktop app.

On a self-hosted server, Processor is only in builds that include it. If there is no **Processor** in the left bar, your build doesn't have it. [Folder scanning](doc:server/storage/folder-scanning) watches server folders without it.

If the button is greyed out with **Ask an admin for processor access**, your account does not have access yet.

## Who can open and manage it

| Action | Stirling Cloud | Self-hosted server |
|---|---|---|
| Open Processor | The team owner. Invited members cannot be given access. | Administrators and team leaders by default. An administrator can [give other users access](doc:server/automation/processor-settings). |
| Create, edit, pause or delete [sources](doc:processor/sources) and [pipelines](doc:processor/pipelines), or start a pipeline with **Run now** | The team owner | Administrators |
| Run a [pipeline](doc:processor/pipelines) on your own files in the editor | Every team member | Every member of the pipeline's team |

Pipelines and sources belong to their owning team. For the other differences on Stirling Cloud, see [Processor and AI on Cloud](doc:cloud/processor-and-ai).

## Credits

Pipeline runs use credits. Manual tools in the editor never do.

- **Stirling Cloud:** runs draw on your team's monthly free credits. For more, the team owner turns on the Processor plan. See [Plans, credits and billing](doc:cloud/plans-and-billing).
- **Self-hosted:** runs use the server's monthly free credits. An administrator can connect the server to a Stirling Cloud team to share that team's allowance; see [Connect to Stirling Cloud](doc:server/licensing/connect-to-stirling-cloud).
