| **Server → Sign-in & security** | Login on or off, login method, lockout, single sign-on, audit logging | [Sign-in and security](doc:server/security/sign-in-and-security) |
| **Server → Integrations** | Mail, Telegram, Google Drive, mobile upload, MCP server | [Telegram bot](doc:server/automation/telegram-bot), [MCP server settings](doc:server/automation/mcp-server) |
| **Server → AI Engine** | Where AI runs, models, limits | [AI on your server](doc:server/ai/ai) |
| **Server → Database** | Connection, backups and restore | [Database](doc:server/storage/database) |
| **Server → Advanced** | Feature flags, processing, temp files, process limits | [Process limits](doc:server/operations/process-limits) |
| **Server → Legal & privacy** | Legal links, login agreement, analytics, search engine visibility | [Analytics and telemetry](doc:server/analytics-and-telemetry) |
| **Monitoring** | **Usage Analytics** and **Audit log** | [Usage monitoring](doc:server/operations/usage-monitoring), [Audit logging](doc:server/security/audit-logging) |

Select **Save Changes**. If a change needs a restart, choose **Restart Now** or **Restart Later**.

With login turned off, the admin pages are greyed out, so use the file or environment variables.

## settings.yml

Edit `settings.yml` and restart to apply changes.

On every start the file is rebuilt from the shipped template, keeping your values:

- A commented-out entry comes back with its default value. To turn something off, change its value instead.
- Keys that aren't in the shipped file are removed. Put them in `custom_settings.yml` or set them as environment variables, like the settings marked * in [Processor server settings](doc:server/automation/processor-settings).
- A file with fewer than 31 lines is treated as invalid: it is saved as `settings.yml.<timestamp>.bak` and replaced with the defaults. Put short overrides in `custom_settings.yml` instead.

## Environment variables

Turn a `settings.yml` path into a variable name: join the levels with underscores, write it in capitals, and drop hyphens.

| settings.yml | Environment variable |
|---|---|
| `security.enableLogin` | `SECURITY_ENABLELOGIN` |
| `security.initialLogin.username` | `SECURITY_INITIALLOGIN_USERNAME` |
| `system.customPaths.operations.soffice` | `SYSTEM_CUSTOMPATHS_OPERATIONS_SOFFICE` |
| `endpoints.toRemove` (a list) | `ENDPOINTS_TOREMOVE`, comma-separated, such as `img-to-pdf,remove-pages` |

The same settings both ways:


  
    ```yaml
    security:
      enableLogin: true
    system:
      defaultLocale: de-DE
    endpoints:
      toRemove: [img-to-pdf, remove-pages]
    ```
  
  
    ```bash
    SECURITY_ENABLELOGIN=true
    SYSTEM_DEFAULTLOCALE=de-DE
    ENDPOINTS_TOREMOVE=img-to-pdf,remove-pages
    ```
  


Restart the container or service after changing a variable.

## Common settings

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `security.enableLogin` | `true` | Require sign-in. |
| `security.initialLogin.username`, `.password` | empty | First admin account. Only used while the database has no users. |
| `system.defaultLocale` | empty | Language for users who haven't picked one, such as `de-DE`. Empty uses the browser language, then `en-US`. |
| `ui.languages` | `[]` (all) | Languages users can choose, such as `["de_DE", "fr_FR"]`. |
| `system.fileUploadLimit` | empty (2000 MB) | Largest upload per request: a number from 0 to 999 plus `KB`, `MB` or `GB`, such as `2GB`. |
| `system.backendUrl`, `system.frontendUrl` | empty | Public addresses of the server and the web app. `backendUrl` is required for SAML single sign-on. `frontendUrl` is used in invite emails, share links, mobile QR codes and the redirect after SAML sign-in, and falls back to `backendUrl`. |
| `system.googlevisibility` | `false` | Let search engines index the server. |
| `system.showUpdate`, `system.showUpdateOnlyAdmin` | `true`, `true` | Show new-version notices, to admins only. |

`SYSTEM_ROOTURIPATH` (environment variable only) serves Stirling PDF under a sub-path such as `/pdf`.

For server options such as port, HTTPS and logging, see [Extra settings](doc:server/customisation/extra-settings).

## File locations

In Docker these folders are at the root of the container (`/configs`, `/logs` and so on), ready to mount as volumes. A JAR creates them in the folder you start it from.

| Folder | Contents |
|---|---|
| `configs/` | `settings.yml`, `custom_settings.yml`, the built-in database (`stirling-pdf-DB-*.mv.db`), automatic database backups in `backup/db/`, and generated keys |
| `logs/` | `info.log`, and `invalid-auths.log` for failed sign-ins (used by [Fail2Ban](doc:server/security/fail2ban)) |
| `customFiles/` | `static/` for [branding](doc:server/customisation/branding) overrides, `signatures/` for [shared signature files](doc:server/security/signing) |
| `pipeline/` | `watchedFolders/` and `finishedFolders/` for [folder scanning](doc:server/storage/folder-scanning) |
| `storage/` | Files users save on the server, when [file storage](doc:server/storage/file-storage) is on |

Back up `configs/` to keep your users, settings and keys. See the [Production checklist](doc:server/production).

server/customisation/branding.title: UI and branding
server/customisation/branding.description: Rename the app, replace its icons and logos, and add your own CSS on a self-hosted Stirling PDF server.
server/customisation/branding.markdown:
## Branding settings

Open **Settings → Server → System → Branding & appearance**, or set the keys in `settings.yml`:

| Field in Settings | Setting | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Navbar Brand** | `ui.appNameNavbar` | empty (`Stirling PDF`) | The browser tab title and the issuer name shown in authenticator apps for two-factor login. Despite the name, it is not shown in the navigation bar, which shows the logo. |
| **Show Update Notifications** | `system.showUpdate` | `true` | Show a notice when a new version is available. |
| **Show Updates to Admins Only** | `system.showUpdateOnlyAdmin` | `true` | Show that notice to admins only. |
| **Hide Google Drive** | `ui.hideDisabledTools.googleDrive` | `false` | Hide the Google Drive button when Google Drive is off. |
| **Hide Mobile Scanner** | `ui.hideDisabledTools.mobileQRScanner` | `false` | Hide the mobile upload button when the mobile scanner is off. |


  
    ```yaml
    ui:
      appNameNavbar: "Acme PDF"
    ```
  
  
    ```bash
    UI_APPNAMENAVBAR="Acme PDF"
    ```
  
  
    ```yaml
    services:
      stirling-pdf:
        environment:
          UI_APPNAMENAVBAR: Acme PDF
    ```
  


The same card also holds the language, upload limit and **Frontend URL** (`system.frontendUrl`) settings described in [Common settings](doc:server/configuration).

## Replace icons and logos

A file in `customFiles/static/` replaces the file the app serves at the same path. In Docker, mount the folder:

```yaml
services:
  stirling-pdf:
    volumes:
      - ./customFiles:/customFiles
```

Brand images are served from `/modern-logo/`, so put your versions in `customFiles/static/modern-logo/` with these exact filenames:

| File | Used for |
|---|---|
| `favicon.ico` | Browser tab icon |
| `logo192.png`, `logo512.png` | App and home screen icons |
| `StirlingPDFLogoNoTextLight.svg`, `StirlingPDFLogoNoTextDark.svg` | Logo mark without text, for light and dark themes |
| `StirlingPDFLogoBlackText.svg`, `StirlingPDFLogoWhiteText.svg`, `StirlingPDFLogoGreyText.svg` | Logo with text, for light, dark and muted backgrounds |
| `logo-tooltip.svg` | Small logo in tooltips |

Other files at the app root, such as `manifest.json`, can be replaced the same way. Restart Stirling PDF after adding a file, then hard-reload the browser.

> **📝 Note**
>
> Some Stirling logos are built into the app and cannot be replaced.


## Add custom CSS

The app does not load a stylesheet from `customFiles` on its own. To add one, serve your own copy of `index.html` that links to it.

1. Put your stylesheet at `customFiles/static/custom.css`. It is served at `/custom.css`, under your [root path](doc:server/customisation/extra-settings) if you set one.
2. Save the app's current page as your own `index.html`, using your server's URL:

   ```bash
   curl --fail --location http://localhost:8080/ --output ./customFiles/static/index.html
   ```

3. In `customFiles/static/index.html`, add this line just before `</head>`:

   ```html
   <link rel="stylesheet" href="/custom.css">
   ```

4. Restart Stirling PDF. The log shows `Using custom index.html from: /customFiles/static/index.html`.

> **⚠️ Warning: Repeat after every upgrade**
>
> `index.html` refers to asset filenames that change with each release, so an old copy breaks the app after an upgrade. Save a fresh copy and add your `<link>` line again every time you upgrade.


For changes CSS cannot make, such as new layouts or components, build your own frontend: see [Set up and run](doc:developers/contributing) and [Build](doc:developers/contributing) in Contributing.

server/customisation/extra-settings.title: Extra settings
server/customisation/extra-settings.description: Use custom_settings.yml for logging, HTTPS, ports, header limits, a sub-path and an outgoing proxy on a self-hosted server.
server/customisation/extra-settings.markdown:
`custom_settings.yml` holds server settings that `settings.yml` does not cover, such as logging, HTTPS and the port. It sits next to `settings.yml` (`/configs/custom_settings.yml` in Docker) and overrides it where both set the same key ([Which setting wins](doc:server/configuration)). Restart Stirling PDF after editing it.

## Logging

```yaml
logging:
  level:
    root: INFO
```

Single sign-on logging is covered on the [OAuth](doc:server/security/oauth-sso) and [SAML](doc:server/security/saml-sso) pages. For other problems, raise one area at a time and set it back afterwards, because debug logging is large and slows the server:

```yaml
logging:
  level:
    stirling.software: DEBUG  # general problems
```

## Port and session length


  
    ```yaml
    server:
      port: 8080
      servlet:
        session:
          timeout: 30m
    ```
  
  
    ```bash
    SERVER_PORT=8080
    SERVER_SERVLET_SESSION_TIMEOUT=30m
    ```
  


Both values shown are the defaults.

## SSL/TLS configuration

Stirling PDF can serve HTTPS itself from a PKCS12 keystore. In production it is usually simpler to put it behind a reverse proxy that handles HTTPS (see [Production checklist](doc:server/production)).


  
    ```yaml
    server:
      port: 8443
      ssl:
        enabled: true
        key-store: file:./configs/keystore.p12
        key-store-password: your-keystore-password
        key-store-type: PKCS12
        key-alias: stirling
    ```
  
  
    ```bash
    SERVER_PORT=8443
    SERVER_SSL_ENABLED=true
    SERVER_SSL_KEYSTORE=file:./configs/keystore.p12
    SERVER_SSL_KEYSTOREPASSWORD=your-keystore-password
    SERVER_SSL_KEYSTORETYPE=PKCS12
    SERVER_SSL_KEYALIAS=stirling
    ```
  
  
    ```yaml
    services:
      stirling-pdf:
        environment:
          SERVER_PORT: 8443
          SERVER_SSL_ENABLED: "true"
          SERVER_SSL_KEYSTORE: file:./configs/keystore.p12
          SERVER_SSL_KEYSTOREPASSWORD: your-keystore-password
          SERVER_SSL_KEYSTORETYPE: PKCS12
          SERVER_SSL_KEYALIAS: stirling
    ```
  


To create a self-signed certificate for testing:

```bash
keytool -genkeypair -alias stirling -keyalg RSA -keysize 2048 -storetype PKCS12 -keystore configs/keystore.p12 -validity 365
```

## Large request headers (HTTP 431)

If sign-in or single sign-on fails with **HTTP 431 Request Header Fields Too Large**, raise the header limit and restart:


  
    ```yaml
    server:
      max-http-request-header-size: 65536
    ```
  
  
    ```bash
    SERVER_MAXHTTPREQUESTHEADERSIZE=65536
    ```
  
  
    ```yaml
    services:
      stirling-pdf:
        environment:
          SERVER_MAXHTTPREQUESTHEADERSIZE: 65536
    ```
  


Try `131072` if the error continues.

## Serve under a sub-path

To serve the app at a path such as `https://example.com/pdf` instead of the domain root, set:

```bash
SYSTEM_ROOTURIPATH=/pdf
```

In Docker, use this variable: the image's health check reads it too. Outside Docker you can instead set `server.servlet.context-path: /pdf` in `custom_settings.yml`.

Also set **Frontend URL** (`system.frontendUrl`) to the full address, for example `https://example.com/pdf`, so links in emails, share links and mobile QR codes include the path.

## Outgoing HTTP(S) proxy

To send the server's outgoing requests, such as licence checks, through a proxy, pass the standard Java proxy options. In Docker, use `JAVA_CUSTOM_OPTS`:

```yaml
services:
  stirling-pdf:
    environment:
      JAVA_CUSTOM_OPTS: "-Dhttp.proxyHost=proxy.example.com -Dhttp.proxyPort=8888 -Dhttps.proxyHost=proxy.example.com -Dhttps.proxyPort=8888 -Dhttp.nonProxyHosts=localhost|127.*|[::1]|10.*|*.svc|*.cluster.local"
```

When running the JAR, put the same `-D` options before `-jar` on the `java` command line.

server/customisation/features-and-endpoi.title: Turn features on or off
server/customisation/features-and-endpoi.description: Remove individual tools or whole groups of tools from the app and API on a self-hosted Stirling PDF server, with every tool and group ID.
server/customisation/features-and-endpoi.markdown:
Remove tools you don't want people to use, or that your server can't run. A removed tool is greyed out in the app (or hidden, see below) and its API endpoint is switched off for everyone on the server.

## Remove tools

In **Settings → Server → System → Endpoint Management**, pick tools under **Disabled Endpoints** or whole groups under **Disabled Endpoint Groups**, then select **Save Changes** and **Restart Now**.

Or set them in configuration. As environment variables, separate values with commas:


  
    ```yaml
    endpoints:
      toRemove:
        - sign
        - add-watermark
      groupsToRemove:
        - LibreOffice
    ```
  
  
    ```bash
    ENDPOINTS_TOREMOVE=sign,add-watermark
    ENDPOINTS_GROUPSTOREMOVE=LibreOffice
    ```
  


IDs and group names are case-sensitive. The same IDs control which tools the [MCP server](doc:server/automation/mcp-server) exposes, and a tool removed here is never available over MCP.

## Hide or grey out removed tools

By default, removed tools stay visible but greyed out. To hide them instead, turn on **Hide unavailable tools by default** and **Hide unavailable conversions by default** under **Settings → Server → System → User Preference Defaults** (`ui.defaultHideUnavailableTools` and `ui.defaultHideUnavailableConversions`). People can change this in their own settings.

## Tool groups

Removing one of these groups removes every tool in it.

| Group | Tool IDs |
|---|---|
| `PageOps` | `add-page-numbers`, `auto-rotate-pdf`, `auto-split-pdf`, `booklet-imposition`, `crop`, `extract-pages`, `merge-pdfs`, `multi-page-layout`, `overlay-pdf`, `pdf-to-single-page`, `rearrange-pages`, `remove-pages`, `rotate-pdf`, `scale-pages`, `split-by-size-or-count`, `split-pages`, `split-pdf-by-chapters`, `split-pdf-by-sections` |
| `Convert` | `cbz-to-pdf`, `eml-to-pdf`, `file-to-pdf`, `html-to-pdf`, `img-to-pdf`, `json-to-pdf`, `markdown-to-pdf`, `pdf-to-cbz`, `pdf-to-csv`, `pdf-to-epub`, `pdf-to-html`, `pdf-to-img`, `pdf-to-json`, `pdf-to-markdown`, `pdf-to-pdfa`, `pdf-to-presentation`, `pdf-to-rtf`, `pdf-to-text`, `pdf-to-ua`, `pdf-to-vector`, `pdf-to-video`, `pdf-to-word`, `pdf-to-xml`, `url-to-pdf`, `vector-to-pdf` |
| `Security` | `accessibility-report`, `add-password`, `add-stamp`, `add-watermark`, `auto-redact`, `cert-sign`, `change-permissions`, `redact`, `remove-cert-sign`, `remove-password`, `sanitize-pdf`, `sign`, `timestamp-pdf`, `unlock-pdf-forms`, `validate-compliance`, `validate-signature`, `verify-pdf` |
| `Other` | `add-attachments`, `add-image`, `batch-process-attachments`, `compare`, `delete-fields`, `edit-table-of-contents`, `extract-images`, `extract-single-attachment`, `fields`, `fill`, `flatten`, `get-info-on-pdf`, `list-attachments`, `modify-fields`, `multi-tool`, `ocr-pdf`, `remove-annotations`, `remove-blanks`, `replace-invert-pdf`, `text-editor-pdf`, `update-metadata`, `view-pdf` |
| `Advance` | `adjust-contrast`, `auto-rename`, `compress-pdf`, `extract-image-scans`, `overlay-pdf`, `repair`, `scanner-effect` |
| `Automation` | `automate`, `handleData`, `pipeline` |
| `DocParse` | `ingest` |
| `DeveloperTools` | `show-javascript` |
| `DeveloperDocs` | `dev-api-docs`, `dev-airgapped-docs`, `dev-folder-scanning-docs`, `dev-sso-guide-docs` (links to developer guides in the app) |

Tools outside these groups, such as `pdf-to-cbr` or `remove-image-pdf`, can still be removed by ID. A tool's ID is the last part of its API path, and conversions use `<from>-to-<to>`, so `/api/v1/convert/pdf/img` is `pdf-to-img`. The [API docs](doc:developers/api) at `/swagger-ui/index.html` on your server list every path.

## Dependency groups

These groups are named after what a tool needs to run. When a program is missing, Stirling PDF removes its group at startup. Tools with another way to run, such as `compress-pdf`, stay available.

| Group | Tools that use it |
|---|---|
| `LibreOffice` | `file-to-pdf`, `pdf-to-html`, `pdf-to-pdfa`, `pdf-to-presentation`, `pdf-to-rtf`, `pdf-to-word`, `pdf-to-xml` |
| `Unoconvert` | `file-to-pdf` |
| `Python` | `extract-image-scans`, `file-to-pdf`, `html-to-pdf`, `url-to-pdf` |
| `OpenCV` | `extract-image-scans` |
| `Weasyprint` | `eml-to-pdf`, `html-to-pdf`, `markdown-to-pdf`, `url-to-pdf` |
| `Calibre` | `pdf-to-epub` |
| `qpdf` | `compress-pdf`, `repair` |
| `Ghostscript` | `compress-pdf`, `crop`, `pdf-to-vector`, `repair`, `replace-invert-pdf`, `scanner-effect`, `vector-to-pdf` |
| `ImageMagick` | `compress-pdf` |
| `OCRmyPDF` | `ocr-pdf` (runs with either `OCRmyPDF` or `tesseract`) |
| `tesseract` | `auto-rotate-pdf`, `ocr-pdf` |
| `Pdftohtml` | `pdf-to-html`, `pdf-to-markdown` |
| `veraPDF` | `accessibility-report`, `pdf-to-ua`, `validate-compliance`, `verify-pdf` |
| `Java` | Built-in tools that need no extra program, such as `merge-pdfs`, `split-pages`, `compress-pdf` and `pdf-to-img`. Removing this group turns off most of the app. |
| `Javascript` | `adjust-contrast`, `compare`, `rearrange-pages`, `sign`, `text-editor-pdf` |
| `rar` | `pdf-to-cbr` (see [PDF to CBR conversion](doc:server/customisation/pdf-to-cbr)) |
| `CLI` | `compress-pdf`, `extract-image-scans`, `file-to-pdf`, `html-to-pdf`, `ocr-pdf`, `pdf-to-html`, `pdf-to-pdfa`, `pdf-to-presentation`, `pdf-to-rtf`, `pdf-to-word`, `pdf-to-xml`, `repair`, `url-to-pdf`. The ultra-lite image removes this group. |

## Tools that are off by default

`url-to-pdf` stays off unless you turn on **Enable URL to PDF** under **Settings → Server → Advanced → Feature Flags** (`system.enableUrlToPDF`). It fetches web pages from your server, so only enable it for trusted internal use.

**Auto Form Detection** (`form-detection`) only runs on the standard and fat Docker images, which ship with a detection model. To install it, open **Settings → Server → System → AI Form Detection** and select **Install** next to the model. For a server without internet access, follow the steps under **Offline / air-gapped install** on the same card. To turn the tool off, switch off **Enable feature** there (`formDetection.enabled`).

server/customisation/mobile-scanner.title: Mobile scanner settings
server/customisation/mobile-scanner.description: Turn phone uploads by QR code on or off and choose how uploaded photos are converted to PDF on a self-hosted server.
server/customisation/mobile-scanner.markdown:
Control the [mobile scanner](doc:tools/guides/mobile-scanner), which lets people scan a QR code and upload photos from their phone. It is on by default.

## Before you start

The QR code sends phones to your server's **Frontend URL** (`system.frontendUrl`), set under **Settings → Server → System → Branding & appearance**. Set it to an address phones can reach, such as `https://pdf.example.com`.

## Settings

Open **Settings → Server → Integrations → Mobile Phone Upload**, or edit `settings.yml`:

| Field in Settings | Setting | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Enable QR Code Upload** | `system.enableMobileScanner` | `true` | Turn phone uploads on or off. |
| **Convert Images to PDF** | `system.mobileScannerSettings.convertToPdf` | `true` | Turn uploaded photos into a PDF. Off keeps the images as they are. |
| **Image Resolution** | `system.mobileScannerSettings.imageResolution` | `full` | `full` keeps the original size; `reduced` scales to at most 1200 px on the longest side. |
| **Page Format** | `system.mobileScannerSettings.pageFormat` | `A4` | `keep` (original image size), `A4` or `letter`. |
| **Stretch to Fit** | `system.mobileScannerSettings.stretchToFit` | `false` | Stretch images to fill the page. Off centres them and keeps their proportions. |

The last three only apply when **Convert Images to PDF** is on.


  
    ```yaml
    system:
      enableMobileScanner: true
      mobileScannerSettings:
        convertToPdf: true
        imageResolution: full
        pageFormat: A4
        stretchToFit: false
    ```
  
  
    ```bash
    SYSTEM_ENABLEMOBILESCANNER=true
    SYSTEM_MOBILESCANNERSETTINGS_CONVERTTOPDF=true
    SYSTEM_MOBILESCANNERSETTINGS_IMAGERESOLUTION=full
    SYSTEM_MOBILESCANNERSETTINGS_PAGEFORMAT=A4
    SYSTEM_MOBILESCANNERSETTINGS_STRETCHTOFIT=false
    ```
  
  
    ```yaml
    services:
      stirling-pdf:
        environment:
          SYSTEM_ENABLEMOBILESCANNER: "true"
          SYSTEM_MOBILESCANNERSETTINGS_CONVERTTOPDF: "true"
          SYSTEM_MOBILESCANNERSETTINGS_IMAGERESOLUTION: full
          SYSTEM_MOBILESCANNERSETTINGS_PAGEFORMAT: A4
          SYSTEM_MOBILESCANNERSETTINGS_STRETCHTOFIT: "false"
    ```
  


## Related settings

- `system.enableMobileSignature` (default `true`) lets people draw a signature on their phone from the Sign tool, using the same QR code flow. It also needs the frontend URL.
- **Hide Mobile Scanner** (`ui.hideDisabledTools.mobileQRScanner`, default `false`) hides the upload button when the scanner is off.

Uploaded files are held in temporary storage on the server and removed once downloaded or after 10 minutes of inactivity.

server/customisation/pdf-to-cbr.title: PDF to CBR conversion
server/customisation/pdf-to-cbr.description: Install the rar program so a self-hosted Stirling PDF server can convert PDFs to CBR comic book files.
server/customisation/pdf-to-cbr.markdown:
Converting PDFs to CBR needs the `rar` command-line program, which Stirling PDF does not ship. At startup, Stirling PDF turns the `pdf-to-cbr` tool on only if it finds `rar` on the `PATH`. PDF to CBZ needs nothing extra.

RAR is shareware that needs a licence after its trial period; see the [RAR licence](https://www.win-rar.com/winrarlicense.html?L=0).

## Install rar


  
    Debian and Ubuntu have `rar` in the `non-free` repository:

    ```bash
    sudo apt install rar
    ```

    Or download "RAR for Linux x64" from [rarlab.com](https://www.rarlab.com/download.htm) and copy the `rar` binary to `/usr/local/bin/`.
  
  
    Download the RAR command line tools from [rarlab.com](https://www.rarlab.com/download.htm) and copy `rar.exe` to a folder on your system `PATH`.
  


Check that the account running Stirling PDF can find it (`which rar` on Linux, `where rar` on Windows), then restart Stirling PDF.

## Docker

The container needs a Linux `rar` binary that matches its architecture. Mount one from the host, or build it into your own image:

```yaml
services:
  stirling-pdf:
    volumes:
      - /usr/local/bin/rar:/usr/local/bin/rar:ro
```

Check it with `docker exec -it <container_name> rar`, then restart the container.

server/faq.title: Server FAQ
server/faq.description: Answers to common questions and problems when running a self-hosted Stirling PDF server.
server/faq.markdown:
## `docker pull` from docker.stirlingpdf.com fails. What now?

Pull the same image from Docker Hub (`stirlingtools/stirling-pdf`) or GitHub (`ghcr.io/stirling-tools/stirling-pdf`) instead. See [Other registries](doc:server/install/docker).

## How do I turn login on or off?

Login is on by default. To turn it off, set this and restart:


  
    ```yaml
    security:
      enableLogin: false
    ```
  
  
    ```bash
    SECURITY_ENABLELOGIN=false
    ```
  


With login off, anyone who can reach the server can use it, and there are no users or single sign-on. See [Sign-in and security](doc:server/security/sign-in-and-security).

## Why does uploading a large file download an .htm file or fail?

Your reverse proxy is rejecting the upload: nginx allows 1 MB by default. Raise its body size limit and timeouts as in the [nginx example](doc:server/production).

## Why does Stirling PDF use so much memory when idle?

- The Docker image sizes the Java heap from the container's memory limit, or from the host's RAM if there is no limit. Set a limit with `mem_limit` or `--memory`.
- `latest-ultra-lite` uses the least memory.

See [Performance](doc:server/operations/performance).

## Why does my server make requests to js.stripe.com?

Only when an admin opens the checkout to buy a plan. No documents are sent to Stripe.

## How do I check the logs?

Run `docker logs stirling-pdf`, or open the `logs` folder (the `/logs` volume in Docker). The first error usually names the cause.

## Getting help

Run [Diagnostics](doc:server/operations/diagnostics) to collect logs and settings into one archive, then see the [FAQ](doc:tools/faq) for where to report the problem.

server/install/docker.title: Install with Docker
server/install/docker.description: Run Stirling PDF in Docker, choose an image, keep your data in volumes and update safely.
server/install/docker.markdown:
Docker is the recommended way to run a Stirling PDF server.

## Quick start




Create `docker-compose.yml`:

```yaml
services:
  stirling-pdf:
    image: docker.stirlingpdf.com/stirlingtools/stirling-pdf:latest
    container_name: stirling-pdf
    ports:
      - '8080:8080'
    volumes:
      - ./stirling-data/configs:/configs
      - ./stirling-data/logs:/logs
      - ./stirling-data/customFiles:/customFiles
      - ./stirling-data/pipeline:/pipeline
      - ./stirling-data/storage:/storage
      - ./stirling-data/tessdata:/usr/share/tessdata
    mem_limit: 4g
    restart: unless-stopped
```

Then start it:

```bash
docker compose up -d
```




```bash
docker run -d \
  --name stirling-pdf \
  -p 8080:8080 \
  -v ./stirling-data/configs:/configs \
  -v ./stirling-data/logs:/logs \
  -v ./stirling-data/customFiles:/customFiles \
  -v ./stirling-data/pipeline:/pipeline \
  -v ./stirling-data/storage:/storage \
  -v ./stirling-data/tessdata:/usr/share/tessdata \
  --memory 4g \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  docker.stirlingpdf.com/stirlingtools/stirling-pdf:latest
```




Open `http://localhost:8080` and sign in as `admin` / `stirling` (see [First login](doc:server/server)).

## Choose an image

| Tag | Login and admin settings | Includes | Suggested memory |
|---|---|---|---|
| `latest` | Yes | LibreOffice, Tesseract, OCRmyPDF, WeasyPrint, Calibre, Ghostscript, QPDF and ImageMagick. No rar, so no PDF to CBR | 4 GB |
| `latest-fat` | Yes | Everything in `latest`, plus the bundled AI engine, which stays off until you [turn it on](doc:server/ai/run-the-ai-engine) | 6 GB, more with AI turned on |
| `latest-ultra-lite` | No | Core PDF tools only. No OCR, Office, HTML or ebook conversions | 2 GB |

Start with `latest`. Switch images by changing the tag and recreating the container. Your volumes carry over.

All images are built for `amd64` and `arm64`.

### Pin a version

`latest` moves with every release. To control when you upgrade, use a version tag instead: `<version>`, `<version>-fat` or `<version>-ultra-lite`. Version numbers are listed on the [releases page](https://github.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-PDF/releases).

### Other registries

The images are also published to Docker Hub and GitHub. Use them if `docker.stirlingpdf.com` is unreachable:

```bash
docker pull stirlingtools/stirling-pdf:latest
docker pull ghcr.io/stirling-tools/stirling-pdf:latest
```

## Volumes

| Container path | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `/configs` | `settings.yml`, `custom_settings.yml`, the built-in database and its backups, and generated keys. Always mount this. |
| `/logs` | Log files. |
| `/customFiles` | Branding overrides and signature files. See [UI and branding](doc:server/customisation/branding). |
| `/pipeline` | Watched and finished folders for [folder scanning](doc:server/storage/folder-scanning). |
| `/storage` | Files users save on the server. [File storage](doc:server/storage/file-storage) is on by default, so always mount this. |
| `/usr/share/tessdata` | Extra OCR language files. See [OCR languages](doc:server/operations/ocr-languages). |

The container runs as UID and GID `1000`. If your host folders belong to another user, set `PUID` and `PGID` to that user's IDs. `UMASK` (default `022`) sets permissions on new files.

## Common settings

Put settings in `/configs/settings.yml`, or pass them as environment variables. Any `settings.yml` key works either way: see [Configuration](doc:server/configuration).


  
    ```yaml
    system:
      defaultLocale: de-DE    # default language for new users
    security:
      enableLogin: false      # run without login
    ```
  
  
    ```bash
    SYSTEM_DEFAULTLOCALE=de-DE
    SECURITY_ENABLELOGIN=false
    ```
  


To serve on another port, change the host side of the mapping, for example `'9000:8080'`.

## Updating Stirling PDF




```bash
docker compose pull
docker compose up -d
```




```bash
docker pull docker.stirlingpdf.com/stirlingtools/stirling-pdf:latest
docker stop stirling-pdf
docker rm stirling-pdf
# then run your original docker run command again
```




Your data stays in the volumes. Back up `/configs` before a major upgrade, and read [Upgrading from V1](doc:server/upgrading/upgrading) if you are coming from V1.

## Platform quick starts

These platforms have community-maintained packages that wrap the Docker image. Report problems with the package to its own project, and Stirling PDF problems to the [issue tracker](https://github.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-PDF/issues).




1. Go to **Apps → Discover Apps** and search for "Stirling PDF".
2. Select **Install**, and change the port or storage if needed.
3. Open it from **Apps → Installed**.

Catalog listing: [apps.truenas.com/catalog/stirling-pdf/](https://apps.truenas.com/catalog/stirling-pdf/).




1. Install the [Community Applications](https://forums.unraid.net/topic/38582-plug-in-community-applications/) plugin if you don't have it.
2. On the **Apps** tab, search for "Stirling PDF" and select **Install**.
3. Check the paths and variables in the template, then select **Apply**.

The template sets `PUID=99` and `PGID=100` for you.




The Community Scripts project has a one-line LXC installer. Run it from the Proxmox VE shell:

```bash
bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/community-scripts/ProxmoxVE/main/ct/stirling-pdf.sh)"
```

When it finishes, open `http://<container-ip>:8080`. Script details: [community-scripts/ProxmoxVE](https://community-scripts.github.io/ProxmoxVE/scripts?id=stirling-pdf).

To run Docker inside an LXC instead, enable nesting (`pct set <ctid> -features nesting=1,keyctl=1`), install Docker and use the compose file above.




Marius Hosting has step-by-step guides for [Synology](https://mariushosting.com/how-to-install-stirling-pdf-on-your-synology-nas/), [UGREEN](https://mariushosting.com/how-to-install-stirling-pdf-on-your-ugreen-nas/) and [Asustor](https://mariushosting.com/how-to-install-stirling-pdf-on-your-asustor-nas/).




- **Portainer:** go to **Stacks → Add stack** and paste the compose file above.
- **CasaOS:** use **Install a customized app** with the image `docker.stirlingpdf.com/stirlingtools/stirling-pdf:latest`, port `8080`, and bind mounts for the [volumes](#volumes).




For rootless Podman with systemd, save this as `~/.config/containers/systemd/stirling-pdf.container`:

```ini
[Unit]
Description=Stirling PDF

[Container]
Image=docker.stirlingpdf.com/stirlingtools/stirling-pdf:latest
PublishPort=8080:8080
Volume=%h/stirling-pdf/configs:/configs:Z
Volume=%h/stirling-pdf/logs:/logs:Z
Volume=%h/stirling-pdf/customFiles:/customFiles:Z
Volume=%h/stirling-pdf/pipeline:/pipeline:Z
Volume=%h/stirling-pdf/storage:/storage:Z
Volume=%h/stirling-pdf/tessdata:/usr/share/tessdata:Z
UserNS=keep-id:uid=1000,gid=1000
AutoUpdate=registry

[Install]
WantedBy=default.target
```

Then run `systemctl --user daemon-reload && systemctl --user start stirling-pdf`.

The `:Z` label is needed on SELinux distributions such as Fedora and RHEL. `UserNS=keep-id` maps your user to the container user, so you don't need `PUID` and `PGID`.




If the container won't start or the page won't load, [check the logs](doc:server/faq).

server/install/jar.title: Install with Java (JAR)
server/install/jar.description: Run the Stirling PDF server as a Java application on Windows, macOS or Linux, with the conversion tools installed yourself.
server/install/jar.markdown:
Run the server as a plain Java application when Docker isn't an option. You install Java and the conversion tools that the [Docker image](doc:server/install/docker) has built in.

## Choose a JAR

| File | Web interface | Login and admin settings | Use it for |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Stirling-PDF-with-login.jar](https://github.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-PDF/releases/latest/download/Stirling-PDF-with-login.jar) | Yes | Yes | Most servers. Recommended. |
| [Stirling-PDF.jar](https://github.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-PDF/releases/latest/download/Stirling-PDF.jar) | Yes | No | One user who needs no login. |
| [Stirling-PDF-server.jar](https://github.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-PDF/releases/latest/download/Stirling-PDF-server.jar) | No | No | API-only use or a custom frontend. |

All three are attached to every [GitHub release](https://github.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-PDF/releases). The examples below use the with-login JAR.

## 1. Install Java 25




Install [Eclipse Temurin 25](https://adoptium.net/temurin/releases/?version=25&os=windows) and let the installer add Java to your PATH.




```bash
brew install openjdk@25
echo 'export PATH="$(brew --prefix openjdk@25)/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.zshrc
```

Open a new terminal afterwards.




```bash
# Debian / Ubuntu
sudo apt-get install -y openjdk-25-jdk
# Fedora
sudo dnf install -y java-25-openjdk
```

If your distribution has no Java 25 package, use [Eclipse Temurin 25](https://adoptium.net/temurin/releases/?version=25).




Check it with `java -version`.

## 2. Download and start the server

Put the JAR in its own folder, open a terminal there and run:

```bash
java -jar Stirling-PDF-with-login.jar
```

Open `http://localhost:8080` and sign in as `admin` / `stirling` (see [First login](doc:server/server)). Others on your network use `http://<server-ip>:8080`.

Stirling PDF keeps its settings, database and logs in folders such as `configs/` and `logs/` inside the folder you start it from, so always start it from the same place. See [Configuration](doc:server/configuration).

### Or use a package manager

These install the with-login JAR and a `stirling-pdf-server` command that starts it.




```powershell
scoop bucket add java
scoop install https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Stirling-Tools/homebrew-stirling-pdf/main/scoop/stirling-pdf-server.json
```

Update with `scoop update stirling-pdf-server`.




```bash
brew tap Stirling-Tools/stirling-pdf
brew install stirling-pdf-server
```

Update with `brew upgrade stirling-pdf-server`.




With [Homebrew on Linux](https://brew.sh/):

```bash
brew tap Stirling-Tools/stirling-pdf
brew install stirling-pdf-server
```




## 3. Install the conversion tools

At startup, Stirling PDF looks for these programs and turns off any tool whose program is missing. The startup log lists what was turned off. Install only what you need, then restart Stirling PDF.

| Program | Enables |
|---|---|
| LibreOffice | Office documents to and from PDF, PDF/A |
| Tesseract or OCRmyPDF | OCR |
| Ghostscript | PDF/X, PostScript to and from PDF, PDF to PCL and XPS, **Replace & Invert Color**, scanner effect, repair and stronger compression |
| QPDF | Repair and stronger compression |
| ImageMagick | The **Convert images to line art** option in **Compress** |
| Python 3 with OpenCV | Detect and split scanned photos |
| WeasyPrint | HTML, Markdown, email and URL to PDF |
| unoserver | Faster Office conversions |
| pdftohtml (Poppler) | PDF to HTML and Markdown |
| Calibre | eBooks to and from PDF |
| rar | PDF to CBR |




1. Install the programs you need:
   - [LibreOffice](https://www.libreoffice.org/download/download-libreoffice/)
   - [Tesseract](https://github.com/UB-Mannheim/tesseract/wiki), choosing extra languages during setup
   - [QPDF](https://qpdf.sourceforge.io/)
   - [Python](https://www.python.org/downloads/), ticking **Add Python to PATH**, then `pip install opencv-python unoserver`
   - [WeasyPrint](https://github.com/Kozea/WeasyPrint/releases): put `weasyprint.exe` in a folder such as `C:\weasyprint`. Some antivirus tools flag it, so you may need to allow it.
   - [pdftohtml](https://sourceforge.net/projects/pdftohtml/): put `pdftohtml.exe` in a folder such as `C:\pdftohtml`
2. Add each program's folder to the system PATH: search Windows for **Edit the system environment variables**, select **Environment Variables**, edit **Path** under **System variables** and add, for example:
   - `C:\Program Files\LibreOffice\program`
   - `C:\Program Files\Tesseract-OCR`
   - `C:\Program Files\qpdf\bin`
   - `C:\weasyprint` and `C:\pdftohtml`
3. Point Stirling PDF at the Tesseract language files in `configs/settings.yml` (or set `SYSTEM_TESSDATADIR`):

   ```yaml
   system:
     tessdataDir: 'C:\Program Files\Tesseract-OCR\tessdata'
   ```

4. Open a new terminal and check each program, for example `tesseract --version` and `python -c "import cv2"`.




```bash
brew install qpdf tesseract tesseract-lang ghostscript imagemagick poppler
brew install --cask libreoffice
pip3 install weasyprint unoserver opencv-python-headless
```

Point Stirling PDF at the Homebrew Tesseract files in `configs/settings.yml` (or set `SYSTEM_TESSDATADIR`). Use the output of `brew --prefix` followed by `/share/tessdata`, for example on Apple Silicon:

```yaml
system:
  tessdataDir: /opt/homebrew/share/tessdata
```




Debian / Ubuntu:

```bash
sudo apt-get install -y libreoffice-writer libreoffice-calc libreoffice-impress python3-uno \
  tesseract-ocr ocrmypdf ghostscript qpdf imagemagick poppler-utils python3-pip
pip3 install unoserver weasyprint opencv-python-headless --break-system-packages
```

Stirling PDF ignores QPDF older than 12 and ImageMagick older than 7, which is what Ubuntu 24.04 and Debian 12 install.

Fedora:

```bash
sudo dnf install -y libreoffice-writer libreoffice-calc libreoffice-impress libreoffice-pyuno \
  tesseract ocrmypdf ghostscript qpdf ImageMagick poppler-utils python3-pip
pip3 install unoserver weasyprint opencv-python-headless
```

Stirling PDF reads Tesseract languages from `/usr/share/tesseract-ocr/5/tessdata`. If your distribution puts them elsewhere, set `system.tessdataDir` in `configs/settings.yml` or the `TESSDATA_PREFIX` environment variable. To add languages, see [OCR languages](doc:server/operations/ocr-languages).




Office conversions work with LibreOffice alone. For faster conversions, also run unoserver next to Stirling PDF, which looks for it on `127.0.0.1:2003`:

```bash
unoserver --port 2003 --interface 127.0.0.1
```

If a program is installed but not on the PATH, set its full path under `system.customPaths.operations` (`soffice`, `unoconvert`, `weasyprint`, `ocrmypdf`, `calibre`) in `settings.yml`.

## Run as a service on Linux

1. Create a user and move the JAR into place:

   ```bash
   sudo useradd --system --home-dir /opt/Stirling-PDF --shell /usr/sbin/nologin stirlingpdf
   sudo mkdir -p /opt/Stirling-PDF
   sudo mv Stirling-PDF-with-login.jar /opt/Stirling-PDF/
   sudo touch /opt/Stirling-PDF/.env
   sudo chown -R stirlingpdf:stirlingpdf /opt/Stirling-PDF
   ```

2. Put any environment variables in `/opt/Stirling-PDF/.env`, one per line, for example `SYSTEM_DEFAULTLOCALE=de-DE`.
3. Create `/etc/systemd/system/stirlingpdf.service`:

   ```ini
   [Unit]
   Description=Stirling PDF
   After=network.target

   [Service]
   User=stirlingpdf
   Group=stirlingpdf
   EnvironmentFile=/opt/Stirling-PDF/.env
   WorkingDirectory=/opt/Stirling-PDF
   ExecStart=/usr/bin/java -jar /opt/Stirling-PDF/Stirling-PDF-with-login.jar
   SuccessExitStatus=143

   [Install]
   WantedBy=multi-user.target
   ```

4. Start it and enable it at boot:

   ```bash
   sudo systemctl daemon-reload
   sudo systemctl enable --now stirlingpdf.service
   sudo systemctl status stirlingpdf.service
   ```

## Change the port or address

Set it in `configs/custom_settings.yml`, or as environment variables, for example in the `.env` file above:


  
    ```yaml
    server:
      address: 0.0.0.0
      port: 3000
    ```
  
  
    ```bash
    SERVER_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0
    SERVER_PORT=3000
    ```
  


## Update

Stop Stirling PDF, replace the JAR with the new release, and start it again. Everything in `configs/` is kept. Back it up first: see the [Production checklist](doc:server/production).

server/install/kubernetes.title: Install on Kubernetes
server/install/kubernetes.description: Install Stirling PDF on Kubernetes with the official Helm chart, keep its data on a persistent volume and upgrade it.
server/install/kubernetes.markdown:
Install Stirling PDF with the official Helm chart:

```bash
helm repo add stirling-pdf https://stirling-tools.github.io/Stirling-PDF-chart
helm repo update
helm install stirling-pdf stirling-pdf/stirling-pdf-chart --namespace stirling-pdf --create-namespace -f values.yaml
```

## values.yaml

Put your overrides in `values.yaml`. The chart's [default values.yaml](https://github.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-PDF-chart/blob/main/charts/stirling-pdf/values.yaml) lists every option with comments.

```yaml
image:
  tag: "3.1.0"           # the chart's default image is an older release

persistence:
  enabled: true

deployment:
  extraVolumeMounts:
    - name: storage-volume   # the volume the chart creates when persistence is enabled
      mountPath: /configs
      subPath: configs
    - name: storage-volume
      mountPath: /storage
      subPath: storage

envs:
  - name: SYSTEM_DEFAULTLOCALE
    value: en-GB
```

- **image.tag:** a version tag pins the release, so you choose when to upgrade. For the fat or ultra-lite image, see [Choose an image](doc:server/install/docker).
- **Persistence:** Stirling PDF keeps users, `settings.yml` and its built-in database in `/configs`, and files users save on the server in `/storage`. Without a persistent volume they are lost when the pod restarts. Enabling persistence creates the volume, and `extraVolumeMounts` mounts a folder of it at each path.
- **envs:** any setting can be passed as an environment variable. See [Configuration](doc:server/configuration) for the naming rule.

Give the pod at least 4 GB of memory with `resources.limits.memory` (see [Sizing](doc:server/operations/performance)). For a sub-path, set the chart's `rootPath` option rather than `SYSTEM_ROOTURIPATH`, so the health checks use it too.

## Upgrade

Change `image.tag` in `values.yaml` to the new version, then run:

```bash
helm repo update
helm upgrade stirling-pdf stirling-pdf/stirling-pdf-chart --namespace stirling-pdf -f values.yaml
```

If you use `latest`, the tag never changes, so `helm upgrade` does not restart the pod or pull the new image. Set `image.pullPolicy: Always` in `values.yaml` and apply it with the command above. After that, restart the pod to upgrade:

```bash
kubectl rollout restart deployment/stirling-pdf-stirling-pdf-chart --namespace stirling-pdf
```

To run several replicas behind one service, see [Clustering](doc:server/operations/clustering).

server/licensing/connect-to-stirling-clo.title: Connect to Stirling Cloud
server/licensing/connect-to-stirling-clo.description: Link a self-hosted server to a Stirling Cloud team to use its plan and processing allowance, and see what the link sends.
server/licensing/connect-to-stirling-clo.markdown:
Link your server to a Stirling Cloud team to use that team's plan, users and processing allowance. Enterprise servers don't need to link.

Linking gives the server:

- The team's Team plan, with no licence key. Linking never grants Enterprise.
- The team's user allowance.
- The team's processing allowance, in place of the server's own 1,000 units a month.
- Access to Stirling Cloud AI. See [Use Stirling Cloud AI from your server](doc:server/ai/use-stirling-cloud-ai).

## Processing allowance

Using the tools by hand never counts. These do:

| Work | Counted as |
|---|---|
| Processor pipelines and policies | Automation |
| [Pipeline API](doc:developers/pipeline-api) steps and [MCP](doc:mcp/mcp) tool calls | Automation |
| AI tools | AI |
| PDF tool calls made with an API key | API |

An unlinked server gets 1,000 units a month. A file uses one unit per 25 pages or per 5 MB, whichever gives more. No file uses more than 1,000 units.

When the units run out, automation, AI and API calls stop until the next month. Manual tools keep working.

A linked server uses the team's allowance and Stirling Cloud's unit rules instead.

Nothing is counted on a server with an Enterprise licence. A Team licence key also makes API tool calls free.

## Connect your server

1. Make sure login is on, then sign in to your server as the organization owner.
2. Open **Settings → Workspace → Account connection** and select **Connect your Stirling account**.
3. Sign in to Stirling Cloud with an account that owns the team you want to use.
4. On **Connect this server?**, check that the **Address** is your server, tick **I recognise this address and want to connect it to my team** and select **Connect server**.
5. Back on your server, check the plan and allowance under **Settings → Workspace → Usage & Billing**.

Only a Cloud team owner can approve a server. If the address doesn't use HTTPS, Stirling Cloud shows **Not an encrypted address**.

## What is sent

[![Your server sends its user count, usage totals and instance details every 24 hours and receives its plan, Team allowance and processing credits.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-Tools.github.io/main/static/img/account-linking-explained.png)](/img/account-linking-explained.png)

When you connect, the server sends its name and address. It then syncs straight away and every 24 hours: it sends its user count, processing-unit totals and instance ID, and gets back the team's plan, user allowance and remaining credits. No PDFs, filenames or user lists are sent.

If the server can't confirm its plan with Stirling Cloud for 3 days, the Team features and processing that come from the link pause until it reconnects. Installed licence keys and your data are not affected.

## Manage or disconnect

- **Account connection** lists this server and the team's other connected servers. **Manage on stirling.com** opens them in Stirling Cloud, where the team owner can rename or remove them (see [Teams](doc:cloud/teams)).
- **Disconnect this instance** stops using the team's plan and allowance. Files on the server are kept.

server/licensing/plans-and-licences.title: Plans and licences
server/licensing/plans-and-licences.description: What Free, Team and Enterprise unlock on a self-hosted server, and how to get, activate and manage a licence.
server/licensing/plans-and-licences.markdown:
A self-hosted server runs on the Free plan until you add Team or Enterprise. Prices are on [stirling.com/pricing](https://stirling.com/pricing). For Stirling Cloud plans, see [Plans, credits and billing](doc:cloud/plans-and-billing).

## What each plan unlocks

| Feature | Free | Team | Enterprise |
|---|---|---|---|
| Users | 5 | 100, more in blocks of 100 | Set by your contract |
| All PDF tools, REST API, [OAuth2 / OIDC single sign-on](doc:server/security/oauth-sso), server certificate [signing](doc:server/security/signing) | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| [External database](doc:server/storage/database) and [clustering](doc:server/operations/clustering) | - | Yes | Yes |
| S3 or database [file storage](doc:server/storage/file-storage) | - | Yes | Yes |
| Prometheus metrics ([usage monitoring](doc:server/operations/usage-monitoring)) | - | Yes | Yes |
| Custom PDF metadata | - | Yes | Yes |
| [SAML2 single sign-on](doc:server/security/saml-sso) | - | - | Yes |
| [Audit logging](doc:server/security/audit-logging) and **Usage Analytics** | - | - | Yes |
| Database backup and import email notifications | - | - | Yes |
| Offline activation with a certificate file | - | - | Yes |

Processor automation and AI tools draw on a monthly processing allowance, except on Enterprise. PDF tool calls made with an API key also count, unless the server has a Team licence key. See [Processing allowance](doc:server/licensing/connect-to-stirling-cloud).

Licences need a login-capable build (`latest`, `latest-fat` or `Stirling-PDF-with-login.jar`). The `latest-ultra-lite` image and the other JARs have no plans or admin settings.

## User limits

- **Free:** 5 users. A server upgraded from V1 keeps its existing user count as the limit if that is higher.
- **Licence key:** the key sets the limit.
- **Linked Cloud team:** the team's purchased users.

When the server reaches its limit, no more users can be added and admins see a notice such as **Team plan needed** or **Your server has more users than your plan covers**. To add a block of users to a Team licence, email support@stirlingpdf.com.

## Get Team or Enterprise

In the app, only the organization owner can buy or activate a plan, and login must be on. There are three ways to get Team:

- **Buy in the app:** open **Settings → Workspace → Usage & Billing**, select **Upgrade** on Team and pay in the Stripe checkout. The licence key is fetched and activated for you, or the app asks you to paste the key from your email.
- **Link to Stirling Cloud:** a server linked to a Cloud team that has the Team plan runs as Team with no key. See [Connect to Stirling Cloud](doc:server/licensing/connect-to-stirling-cloud).
- **Licence key:** if you bought Team outside the app, activate the key from your email as below.

Enterprise is sold by the Stirling team: [book a demo](https://stirling.com/book-a-demo) or email support@stirlingpdf.com. You get a licence key, or a certificate file for servers without internet access. Linking to Stirling Cloud never grants Enterprise.

## Activating your license

1. Sign in as the organization owner and open **Settings → Workspace → Usage & Billing**.
2. Select **Got a license key or certificate file?**
3. Choose **License Key** and paste your key, or choose **Certificate File**, select **Choose License File** and pick your `.lic` or `.cert` file.
4. Select **Save Changes**.

The plan applies straight away, with no restart. Replacing an existing key can't be undone, so keep a copy of it.

A licence key is checked online. A certificate file works offline: it must start with `-----BEGIN LICENSE FILE-----`, and the server saves it in `configs/`, keeping a copy of any file it replaces in `configs/backup/`.

### Set the licence in settings.yml

For scripted deployments, set the key and restart:


  
    ```yaml
    premium:
      enabled: true
      key: your-licence-key
    ```
  
  
    ```bash
    PREMIUM_ENABLED=true
    PREMIUM_KEY=your-licence-key
    ```
  


For a certificate file, put it in the config folder and point to it with the `file:` prefix, for example `key: file:configs/licence.lic`.

## Billing and the organization owner

- **Invoices, payment method and cancelling:** on **Settings → Workspace → Usage & Billing**, select **Manage** on your current plan to open the Stripe billing portal. Stripe may email you a sign-in link first.
- **Team through a linked Cloud team:** manage the plan in Stirling Cloud. See [Plans, credits and billing](doc:cloud/plans-and-billing).

Only the organization owner can manage **Usage & Billing** and the link to Stirling Cloud. The owner is the first admin account. To hand it over, open **Settings → Workspace → Users**, set another user's role to **Org Owner** and confirm **Transfer ownership**. The new owner becomes an admin.

server/operations/clustering.title: Clustering
server/operations/clustering.description: Run several Stirling PDF nodes behind a load balancer so the service keeps working when a node is lost.
server/operations/clustering.markdown:
Run more than one Stirling PDF node behind a load balancer.

## Prerequisites

- A Team or Enterprise licence.
- Shared by every node: one [external database](doc:server/storage/database), one Valkey (or Redis) server, an S3-compatible bucket for job results, and a load balancer with session affinity. Persistent uploads must use S3 or database [file storage](doc:server/storage/file-storage).
- Valkey running with `maxmemory-policy noeviction`. Any eviction policy can drop live locks and node registrations.
- The same secrets on every node:
  - `STIRLING_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, a base64 256-bit key made once with `openssl rand -base64 32`. A clustered node refuses to start without it. See [Processor server settings](doc:server/automation/processor-settings).
  - `AUTOMATICALLYGENERATED_KEY` and `AUTOMATICALLYGENERATED_UUID`, copied from `AutomaticallyGenerated` in the first node's `settings.yml`. Otherwise nodes cannot read each other's data or agree on licence seat counts.
- A bucket lifecycle rule that expires objects under `cluster.s3.keyPrefix` (default `transient/`) after longer than `stirling.jobResultExpiryMinutes` (default `30`).

## Settings


  
    ```yaml
    cluster:
      enabled: true
      backplane: valkey
      artifactStore: s3
      valkey:
        url: "redis://valkey:6379"
    ```
  
  
    ```bash
    CLUSTER_ENABLED=true
    CLUSTER_BACKPLANE=valkey
    CLUSTER_ARTIFACTSTORE=s3
    CLUSTER_VALKEY_URL=redis://valkey:6379
    ```
  


| Setting | Env | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cluster.enabled` | `CLUSTER_ENABLED` | `false` | Turn clustering on. |
| `cluster.backplane` | `CLUSTER_BACKPLANE` | `inprocess` | Set to `valkey` for more than one node. |
| `cluster.artifactStore` | `CLUSTER_ARTIFACTSTORE` | `local` | Must be `s3` for more than one node. Uses the `storage.s3.*` bucket and credentials. |
| `cluster.valkey.mode` | `CLUSTER_VALKEY_MODE` | empty | `standalone`, `sentinel` or `cluster`. Empty works it out from which settings you filled in. |
| `cluster.valkey.url` | `CLUSTER_VALKEY_URL` | empty | Standalone only: `redis://[user:password@]host[:port]`, or `rediss://` for TLS. Percent-encode `@ : / # ?` in the password. |
| `cluster.valkey.sentinel.master`, `cluster.valkey.sentinel.nodes` | `CLUSTER_VALKEY_SENTINEL_MASTER`, `CLUSTER_VALKEY_SENTINEL_NODES` | empty | Sentinel mode: the monitored primary's name and the sentinels, such as `sentinel-1:26379`. |
| `cluster.valkey.nodes` | `CLUSTER_VALKEY_NODES` | empty | Valkey cluster mode: the cluster nodes, such as `valkey-1:6379`. |
| `cluster.valkey.tls.enabled` | `CLUSTER_VALKEY_TLS_ENABLED` | `false` | TLS for sentinel and cluster modes. |
| `cluster.valkey.tls.skipCertVerification` | `CLUSTER_VALKEY_TLS_SKIPCERTVERIFICATION` | `false` | Skip certificate checks. Development only. |
| `cluster.node.internalAddress` | `CLUSTER_NODE_INTERNALADDRESS` | empty | `host:port` other nodes use to reach this one. Falls back to `POD_IP`, then the hostname's address; the node stops if none works. |

A standalone Valkey is a single point of failure: no node starts while it is down. Use sentinel or cluster mode for high availability.

## Health checks

- `GET /actuator/health` needs no sign-in. It returns HTTP 503 with `"status": "DOWN"` when the node cannot reach Valkey, so use it for load balancer checks. It also reports `DOWN` if another dependency, such as the database, fails.
- `GET /api/v1/info/status` needs no sign-in and always returns `{"status": "UP"}` while the app is running. Use it as a simple liveness check.
- If Valkey is unreachable, job and file requests return HTTP 503.

## Limits

- Job results live on the node that ran the job. A request for them on another node returns HTTP 410, which is why session affinity is required.
- Per-user rate limits are counted once across the whole cluster, through Valkey.
- Pause Processor work before restarting a node. A restart interrupts documents that Processor is handling across the cluster.

server/operations/diagnostics.title: Diagnostics
server/operations/diagnostics.description: Collect logs, configuration and system details from a Stirling PDF Docker container into one archive for troubleshooting or a bug report.
server/operations/diagnostics.markdown:
The Docker images include a diagnostics tool that gathers logs, configuration, system information and app metrics into one archive. Attach it when you report a problem; see the [FAQ](doc:tools/faq) for where to get help.

## Run the tool

```bash
docker exec -it <container_name> diag
```

The tool needs an interactive terminal, so keep the `-it` flags.

Choose a mode when prompted:

- **1) Auto** collects the last day of logs, `/configs`, system information, and the app's status, health and metrics endpoints. It does not redact anything.
- **2) Custom** asks what to include and whether to redact.

PDFs, images and archives are never collected.

### Custom mode options

| Prompt | Default | Collects |
|---|---|---|
| Output directory | `/configs` | Where to save the archive. |
| Days of logs to include | `1` | Log files from this many days. |
| Include /configs? | Yes | Configuration files, such as `settings.yml`. |
| Include /customFiles (excluding PDFs)? | No | Your custom files. |
| Include /pipeline (excluding PDFs)? | No | Pipeline working files. |
| Include /tmp/stirling-pdf? | No | Temporary processing files. |
| Include system information? | Yes | OS, CPU, memory, disk, Java and Python versions. |
| Include environment variables? | No | Every environment variable. |
| Fetch app status/health/metrics endpoints? | Yes | Status, health and load data. |
| Include /api/v1/ui-data endpoints? | No | Data the app's sign, pipeline and OCR screens use. |
| Redact sensitive information from diagnostics? | Yes | Then asks separately about secrets, tokens and passwords (default yes), URL hosts, email addresses, and host, domain and server fields (default no). |

> **⚠️ Caution**
>
> Configuration files and environment variables can contain passwords and keys. Before sharing a bundle publicly, for example in a GitHub issue, run Custom mode with redaction on and check the archive yourself: redaction can miss values.


## Get the archive

The tool prints the archive path when it finishes, in a `Created tar.gz` line. Copy it out of the container:

```bash
docker cp <container_name>:/configs/stirling-diagnostics-20260917-120000.tar.gz ./
```

The archive holds `summary.txt` (what was collected, and the version) and a `bundle/` folder with the collected files.

## AOT diagnostics

If you run with ahead-of-time compilation on (`STIRLING_AOT_ENABLE=true`), `aot-diag` (or `aot-diagnostics`) checks why the AOT cache fails to build, which mostly happens on ARM64. It checks cache integrity and JVM compatibility and can run smoke tests:

```bash
docker exec -it <container_name> aot-diag
```

server/operations/libreoffice.title: LibreOffice parallel processing
server/operations/libreoffice.description: Run several LibreOffice workers, locally or in separate containers, so a self-hosted server converts office documents in parallel.
server/operations/libreoffice.markdown:
Office conversions (Word, Excel, PowerPoint and similar, to and from PDF) run through LibreOffice, and each conversion uses one CPU core. By default only one runs at a time. To convert several documents at once, run more LibreOffice workers.

## Local workers

In the Docker images, Stirling PDF starts its own workers on the first office conversion and stops them after 2 minutes idle. Change the idle time with `UNO_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, or set `UNO_DEMAND_ENABLED=false` to keep them running. Without Docker, start the workers yourself as shown in [Workers without Docker](#workers-without-docker).

Set the pool size with `libreOfficeSessionLimit`:


  
    ```yaml
    processExecutor:
      autoUnoServer: true
      sessionLimit:
        libreOfficeSessionLimit: 4
    ```
  
  
    ```bash
    PROCESS_EXECUTOR_AUTO_UNO_SERVER=true
    PROCESS_EXECUTOR_SESSION_LIMIT_LIBRE_OFFICE_SESSION_LIMIT=4
    ```
  
  
    ```yaml
    services:
      stirling-pdf:
        environment:
          PROCESS_EXECUTOR_AUTO_UNO_SERVER: "true"
          PROCESS_EXECUTOR_SESSION_LIMIT_LIBRE_OFFICE_SESSION_LIMIT: 4
    ```
  


Start with one worker per two CPU cores. With `UNO_DEMAND_ENABLED=false`, each extra worker adds about 50 MB of memory while idle, and more while converting.

## Remote workers

To scale further, or to keep LibreOffice out of the main container, run workers as separate containers from `ghcr.io/stirling-tools/stirling-unoserver`. Each container is one worker listening on port `2003`.

Add the workers next to your `stirling-pdf` service:

```yaml
services:
  unoserver1:
    image: ghcr.io/stirling-tools/stirling-unoserver:latest
  unoserver2:
    image: ghcr.io/stirling-tools/stirling-unoserver:latest
```

Publish a port (for example `"2004:2003"`) only if Stirling PDF runs outside Docker, on another host or on another Docker network.

Then turn off the local pool, list the workers and restart Stirling PDF. As environment variables, number each worker from `0`:


  
    ```yaml
    processExecutor:
      autoUnoServer: false
      sessionLimit:
        libreOfficeSessionLimit: 2
      unoServerEndpoints:
        - host: unoserver1
          port: 2003
          hostLocation: remote
        - host: unoserver2
          port: 2003
          hostLocation: remote
    ```
  
  
    ```bash
    PROCESS_EXECUTOR_AUTO_UNO_SERVER=false
    PROCESS_EXECUTOR_SESSION_LIMIT_LIBRE_OFFICE_SESSION_LIMIT=2
    PROCESS_EXECUTOR_UNO_SERVER_ENDPOINTS_0_HOST=unoserver1
    PROCESS_EXECUTOR_UNO_SERVER_ENDPOINTS_0_PORT=2003
    PROCESS_EXECUTOR_UNO_SERVER_ENDPOINTS_0_HOST_LOCATION=remote
    PROCESS_EXECUTOR_UNO_SERVER_ENDPOINTS_1_HOST=unoserver2
    PROCESS_EXECUTOR_UNO_SERVER_ENDPOINTS_1_PORT=2003
    PROCESS_EXECUTOR_UNO_SERVER_ENDPOINTS_1_HOST_LOCATION=remote
    ```
  
  
    ```yaml
    services:
      stirling-pdf:
        environment:
          PROCESS_EXECUTOR_AUTO_UNO_SERVER: "false"
          PROCESS_EXECUTOR_SESSION_LIMIT_LIBRE_OFFICE_SESSION_LIMIT: 2
          PROCESS_EXECUTOR_UNO_SERVER_ENDPOINTS_0_HOST: unoserver1
          PROCESS_EXECUTOR_UNO_SERVER_ENDPOINTS_0_PORT: 2003
          PROCESS_EXECUTOR_UNO_SERVER_ENDPOINTS_0_HOST_LOCATION: remote
          PROCESS_EXECUTOR_UNO_SERVER_ENDPOINTS_1_HOST: unoserver2
          PROCESS_EXECUTOR_UNO_SERVER_ENDPOINTS_1_PORT: 2003
          PROCESS_EXECUTOR_UNO_SERVER_ENDPOINTS_1_HOST_LOCATION: remote
    ```
  


Every listed worker is used. Set `libreOfficeSessionLimit` to the number of workers to avoid a startup warning. It also caps conversions that fall back to running LibreOffice directly.

### Worker settings

| Field | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `host` | `127.0.0.1` | Docker service name, hostname or IP address. |
| `port` | `2003` | Worker port. |
| `hostLocation` | `auto` | `remote` sends files over the network; `local` passes file paths and only works when the worker shares the filesystem. Use `remote` for separate containers, even on the same machine. |
| `protocol` | `http` | `http` or `https`. |

### The stirling-unoserver image

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `UNOSERVER_PORT` | `2003` | Listen port. |
| `UNOSERVER_INTERFACE` | `0.0.0.0` | Listen address. `127.0.0.1` restricts it to the same host. |
| `UNOSERVER_CONVERSION_TIMEOUT` | `1800` | Longest conversion, in seconds. Keep it in line with [`libreOfficetimeoutMinutes`](doc:server/operations/process-limits) (30 minutes by default). |
| `UNOSERVER_RECYCLE_INTERVAL_SECONDS` | `0` (off) | Restart LibreOffice on a schedule to limit memory growth, for example `3600` for hourly. Minimum 60. |
| `UNOSERVER_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `0` (off) | Stop the worker after this many idle seconds. Keep it at `0` for remote workers, because nothing can start them again. |

For Chinese, Japanese and Korean documents, build the image with `--build-arg INSTALL_CJK_FONTS=true` (about 120 MB larger).

## Workers without Docker

On a bare-metal server, start workers with the `unoserver` Python package, giving each its own ports:

```bash
pip install unoserver
unoserver --port 2003 --uno-port 2103 &
unoserver --port 2004 --uno-port 2104 &
```

Then list them as endpoints on `127.0.0.1` with `hostLocation: local`.

server/operations/ocr-languages.title: OCR languages
server/operations/ocr-languages.description: Add Tesseract language packs to a self-hosted Stirling PDF server so the OCR tool can read more languages.
server/operations/ocr-languages.markdown:
The [OCR tool](doc:tools/guides/ocr) can only offer languages whose Tesseract language pack is installed on the server. The standard Docker images include English, German, French, Portuguese and Simplified Chinese. The ultra-lite image has no OCR.

Stirling PDF uses OCRmyPDF when it is installed, as it is in the standard and fat images, and falls back to Tesseract alone otherwise. The OCR tool's **Processing Options** only work with OCRmyPDF.

## Download languages in the app

1. Open **Settings → Server → Advanced**. The **Processing** card shows the **Tessdata Directory** and its installed languages.
2. Under **Download additional tessdata languages**, pick the languages, then select **Download selected languages**.

The server downloads them from the [tesseract-ocr/tessdata](https://github.com/tesseract-ocr/tessdata) repository, so it needs internet access. If the folder is not writable, the app gives you download links instead; save the files into the tessdata folder yourself.

In Docker, the tessdata folder is inside the container, so languages downloaded this way are lost when the container is recreated. Use a volume, below, for languages you want to keep.

## Add languages with a Docker volume

1. Download the `.traineddata` files you need from [tessdata](https://github.com/tesseract-ocr/tessdata) (more accurate, larger) or [tessdata_fast](https://github.com/tesseract-ocr/tessdata_fast) (faster, smaller).
2. Put them in a host folder and mount it at `/usr/share/tessdata`:

   ```yaml
   services:
     stirling-pdf:
       volumes:
         - ./tessdata:/usr/share/tessdata
   ```

3. Restart the container.

At startup, files in `/usr/share/tessdata` are copied into Tesseract's own folder, `/usr/share/tesseract-ocr/5/tessdata`. Files already there are not replaced.

## Add languages without Docker


  
    ```bash
    sudo apt install tesseract-ocr-spa      # one language (Spanish)
    apt search tesseract-ocr-               # list available languages
    ```
  
  
    ```bash
    sudo dnf install tesseract-langpack-spa # one language (Spanish)
    dnf search tesseract-langpack-          # list available languages
    ```
  
  
    1. Download the `.traineddata` files from [tessdata](https://github.com/tesseract-ocr/tessdata) or [tessdata_fast](https://github.com/tesseract-ocr/tessdata_fast).
    2. Put them in the `tessdata` folder of your Tesseract install, such as `C:\Program Files\Tesseract-OCR\tessdata`, and check with `tesseract --list-langs`.
    3. Point Stirling PDF at that folder in `settings.yml`, then restart:

       ```yaml
       system:
         tessdataDir: C:/Program Files/Tesseract-OCR/tessdata
       ```
  


Keep `eng.traineddata` in the folder: English is always needed.

The tessdata folder is chosen in this order: `system.tessdataDir`, then the `TESSDATA_PREFIX` environment variable, then `/usr/share/tesseract-ocr/5/tessdata`.

server/operations/performance.title: Performance
server/operations/performance.description: Size CPU, memory and disk for a self-hosted Stirling PDF server and tune its memory use.
server/operations/performance.markdown:
PDF processing is memory-hungry: a single large PDF can take many times its file size in memory while it is processed.

## Sizing

| Users | CPU | Memory | Disk |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1-10 | 2-4 cores | 4 GB | 10 GB |
| 10-50 | 4-8 cores | 8-16 GB | 50 GB, SSD recommended |
| 50+ | 8+ cores | 16 GB or more | 100 GB+, SSD |

When a server runs out of memory the container stops and every running job fails, so keep `restart: unless-stopped` set.

Set a memory limit on the container so Stirling PDF can size itself (see below):

```yaml
services:
  stirling-pdf:
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 4G
          cpus: '4.0'
```

Some tools cost far more than others:

| Tool | CPU | Memory |
|---|---|---|
| Merge, split | Low | Grows with total file size |
| OCR | Very high | High |
| Office conversions (LibreOffice) | High, one core per conversion | High |
| PDF to image | Moderate | Very high |
| PDF/A conversion, compression | Moderate | High |

If your users mostly OCR or convert office files, size up and raise the matching [process limits](doc:server/operations/process-limits). To run several office conversions at once, see [LibreOffice parallel processing](doc:server/operations/libreoffice). For several servers, see [Clustering](doc:server/operations/clustering).

## Java memory

The Docker image sets the Java heap automatically from the container's memory limit, up to 70% of it, leaving the rest for LibreOffice, Tesseract and other tools. Without a limit it sizes from the host's total RAM, so always set one.

If the container stops under heavy load, give the other tools more room by lowering the heap to 50%:

```yaml
services:
  stirling-pdf:
    environment:
      JAVA_CUSTOM_OPTS: "-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=50"
```

For a fixed heap size, use `-Xmx2g` in `JAVA_CUSTOM_OPTS` instead. Do not use `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS`, which the image overwrites. When running the JAR, pass `-Xmx2g` to `java` directly. Either way, leave at least a third of the machine's or container's memory outside the heap for the other tools.

server/operations/process-limits.title: Process limits
server/operations/process-limits.description: Set how many copies of each external program run at once and how long each may run on a self-hosted Stirling PDF server.
server/operations/process-limits.markdown:
Some tools run external programs such as LibreOffice, Tesseract or Ghostscript. For each program you can set:

- **Session limit**: how many copies run at once. Extra jobs wait in a queue.
- **Timeout**: how many minutes one run may take before it is stopped and returns an error.

Change them under **Settings → Server → Advanced → Process Executor Limits**, or under `processExecutor` in `settings.yml`. A value of `0` or less uses the default. Restart Stirling PDF after editing the file.

## Session limits

| Setting | Default | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `libreOfficeSessionLimit` | `1` | Office documents to and from PDF |
| `tesseractSessionLimit` | `1` | OCR with Tesseract |
| `ocrMyPdfSessionLimit` | `2` | OCR with OCRmyPDF |
| `pdfToHtmlSessionLimit` | `1` | PDF to HTML and Markdown |
| `ghostscriptSessionLimit` | `8` | Compression, repair and other Ghostscript tools |
| `qpdfSessionLimit` | `4` in `settings.yml`, `2` if unset | PDF/A conversion, repair and compression |
| `imageMagickSessionLimit` | `4` | Line-art conversion in Compress |
| `pythonOpenCvSessionLimit` | `8` | Image processing, such as scan extraction |
| `weasyPrintSessionLimit` | `16` | HTML to PDF |
| `calibreSessionLimit` | `1` | E-book conversion |
| `installAppSessionLimit` | `1` | Internal install tasks |

Raise limits on a large server with many users. Lower them on a small one: each copy uses its own memory and CPU, and LibreOffice is especially memory-hungry. For more LibreOffice capacity, see [LibreOffice parallel processing](doc:server/operations/libreoffice).

## Timeouts

All timeouts are in minutes and default to `30`, except `pdfToHtmltimeoutMinutes` (`20`) and `installApptimeoutMinutes` (`60`). The keys in `settings.yml` are:

`libreOfficetimeoutMinutes`, `pdfToHtmltimeoutMinutes`, `pythonOpenCvtimeoutMinutes`, `weasyPrinttimeoutMinutes`, `installApptimeoutMinutes`, `calibretimeoutMinutes`, `imageMagickTimeoutMinutes`, `tesseractTimeoutMinutes`, `qpdfTimeoutMinutes`, `ghostscriptTimeoutMinutes` and `ocrMyPdfTimeoutMinutes`.

Frequent timeouts usually mean the server is short of CPU or memory.

## Example

A small, low-memory server:


  
    ```yaml
    processExecutor:
      sessionLimit:
        libreOfficeSessionLimit: 1
        tesseractSessionLimit: 1
        ghostscriptSessionLimit: 2
        imageMagickSessionLimit: 2
        pythonOpenCvSessionLimit: 2
        weasyPrintSessionLimit: 4
        qpdfSessionLimit: 1
        ocrMyPdfSessionLimit: 1
      timeoutMinutes:
        libreOfficetimeoutMinutes: 10
        tesseractTimeoutMinutes: 15
    ```
  
  
    ```bash
    PROCESSEXECUTOR_SESSIONLIMIT_LIBREOFFICESESSIONLIMIT=1
    PROCESSEXECUTOR_SESSIONLIMIT_TESSERACTSESSIONLIMIT=1
    PROCESSEXECUTOR_SESSIONLIMIT_GHOSTSCRIPTSESSIONLIMIT=2
    PROCESSEXECUTOR_SESSIONLIMIT_IMAGEMAGICKSESSIONLIMIT=2
    PROCESSEXECUTOR_SESSIONLIMIT_PYTHONOPENCVSESSIONLIMIT=2
    PROCESSEXECUTOR_SESSIONLIMIT_WEASYPRINTSESSIONLIMIT=4
    PROCESSEXECUTOR_SESSIONLIMIT_QPDFSESSIONLIMIT=1
    PROCESSEXECUTOR_SESSIONLIMIT_OCRMYPDFSESSIONLIMIT=1
    PROCESSEXECUTOR_TIMEOUTMINUTES_LIBREOFFICETIMEOUTMINUTES=10
    PROCESSEXECUTOR_TIMEOUTMINUTES_TESSERACTTIMEOUTMINUTES=15
    ```
  
  
    ```yaml
    services:
      stirling-pdf:
        environment:
          PROCESSEXECUTOR_SESSIONLIMIT_LIBREOFFICESESSIONLIMIT: 1
          PROCESSEXECUTOR_SESSIONLIMIT_TESSERACTSESSIONLIMIT: 1
          PROCESSEXECUTOR_SESSIONLIMIT_GHOSTSCRIPTSESSIONLIMIT: 2
          PROCESSEXECUTOR_SESSIONLIMIT_IMAGEMAGICKSESSIONLIMIT: 2
          PROCESSEXECUTOR_SESSIONLIMIT_PYTHONOPENCVSESSIONLIMIT: 2
          PROCESSEXECUTOR_SESSIONLIMIT_WEASYPRINTSESSIONLIMIT: 4
          PROCESSEXECUTOR_SESSIONLIMIT_QPDFSESSIONLIMIT: 1
          PROCESSEXECUTOR_SESSIONLIMIT_OCRMYPDFSESSIONLIMIT: 1
          PROCESSEXECUTOR_TIMEOUTMINUTES_LIBREOFFICETIMEOUTMINUTES: 10
          PROCESSEXECUTOR_TIMEOUTMINUTES_TESSERACTTIMEOUTMINUTES: 15
    ```

server/operations/usage-monitoring.title: Usage monitoring
server/operations/usage-monitoring.description: Check the status and request counts of a self-hosted Stirling PDF server through its info API, the in-app dashboard or Prometheus.
server/operations/usage-monitoring.markdown:
Watch a self-hosted server's health and usage with the built-in info API (all plans), the **Usage Analytics** dashboard (Enterprise) or Prometheus (Team and Enterprise).

## Info API

These endpoints return JSON. With login on, every endpoint except `/api/v1/info/status` needs authentication; from scripts, send an API key in the `X-API-KEY` header.

| Endpoint | Returns |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/v1/info/status` | Status and version. Use it for health checks. |
| `GET /api/v1/info/health` | The same as `status`. |
| `GET /api/v1/info/uptime` | Time since the server started. |
| `GET /api/v1/info/requests` | POST request count, for one endpoint with `?endpoint=` or for all. |
| `GET /api/v1/info/requests/all` | POST request counts for every endpoint. |
| `GET /api/v1/info/load`, `GET /api/v1/info/load/all` | The same, for GET requests. |
| Any `requests` or `load` endpoint plus `/unique` | Unique sessions instead of requests, for example `/api/v1/info/requests/all/unique`. |
| `GET /api/v1/info/wau` | Weekly active users. Only when login is off. |

Counts reset when the server restarts. To turn off everything except `status` and `health`, set `metrics.enabled: false` (`METRICS_ENABLED=false`); the other endpoints then return HTTP 403.

## Usage Analytics dashboard

With an Enterprise licence and login on, admins can see usage in the app under **Settings → Monitoring → Usage Analytics**.

## Prometheus

With a Team or Enterprise licence, Stirling PDF can publish Prometheus metrics: HTTP request counts by endpoint, method and session. Below Team, `/actuator/*` returns HTTP 404 apart from health checks.

Turn the endpoint on in `custom_settings.yml` (see [Extra settings](doc:server/customisation/extra-settings)) or `JAVA_CUSTOM_OPTS`, then restart:


  
    ```yaml
    management:
      endpoints:
        web:
          exposure:
            include: prometheus,health,info
      endpoint:
        health:
          show-details: always
      prometheus:
        metrics:
          export:
            enabled: true
    ```
  
  
    ```bash
    JAVA_CUSTOM_OPTS="-Dmanagement.endpoints.web.exposure.include=prometheus,health,info -Dmanagement.endpoint.health.show-details=always -Dmanagement.prometheus.metrics.export.enabled=true"
    ```
  
  
    ```yaml
    services:
      stirling-pdf:
        environment:
          JAVA_CUSTOM_OPTS: "-Dmanagement.endpoints.web.exposure.include=prometheus,health,info -Dmanagement.endpoint.health.show-details=always -Dmanagement.prometheus.metrics.export.enabled=true"
    ```
  


Then point Prometheus at `/actuator/prometheus`. With login on, it must send an API key in the `X-API-KEY` header:

```yaml
scrape_configs:
  - job_name: 'stirling-pdf'
    metrics_path: '/actuator/prometheus'
    scrape_interval: 15s
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['your-stirling-pdf-host:8080']
```

server/production.title: Production checklist

server/security/audit-logging.title: Audit logging
server/security/audit-logging.description: Record who ran which tool on which files, choose how much to log and how long to keep it, and review the log in Settings.
server/security/audit-logging.markdown:
Record every operation on your server: who ran it, which tool, which files and when. The full audit log needs an Enterprise licence.

Records are stored in the server's database. At high volume, use an [external database](doc:server/storage/database).

Without Enterprise, the server still records document processing for the Processor's [Documents](doc:processor/documents) page and keeps those records for at most 30 days. Turning audit logging off also stops these records.

## Turn it on

Change the settings in **Settings → Server → Sign-in & security → Audit Logging**, or under `premium.enterpriseFeatures.audit`:


  
    ```yaml
    premium:
      enterpriseFeatures:
        audit:
          enabled: true
          level: 2
          retentionDays: 90
          captureFileHash: false
          capturePdfAuthor: false
          captureOperationResults: false
    ```
  
  
    ```bash
    PREMIUM_ENTERPRISEFEATURES_AUDIT_ENABLED=true
    PREMIUM_ENTERPRISEFEATURES_AUDIT_LEVEL=2
    PREMIUM_ENTERPRISEFEATURES_AUDIT_RETENTIONDAYS=90
    PREMIUM_ENTERPRISEFEATURES_AUDIT_CAPTUREFILEHASH=false
    PREMIUM_ENTERPRISEFEATURES_AUDIT_CAPTUREPDFAUTHOR=false
    PREMIUM_ENTERPRISEFEATURES_AUDIT_CAPTUREOPERATIONRESULTS=false
    ```
  


| Setting | In the app | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | **Enable Audit Logging** | `true` | Turn audit logging on or off. |
| `level` | **Audit Level** | `2` | How much to record (see below). |
