- **Change Metadata** - edit the standard fields (author, title, subject, keywords, creator, producer, creation and modification dates), add your own fields under **Custom Metadata**, or tick **Delete all metadata** to strip them.
- **Edit Table of Contents** - add, nest and reorder bookmarks in the **Bookmark editor**. Click **Load from selected PDF** to start from the existing bookmarks, and use **Import JSON** or **Download JSON** to reuse an outline. Click **Apply table of contents** to save.

tools/guides/convert.title: Convert
tools/guides/convert.description: Convert Office files, images, web pages, email, eBooks and comics to PDF, and PDFs to other formats.
tools/guides/convert.markdown:
## Convert a file

1. Select one or more files and open **Convert**.
2. **Convert from** is filled in from the files you selected. Pick the target format under **Convert to**.
3. Set any options for that conversion, then click **Convert Files**.

If you select files of different types, they are all converted to PDF.

## Convert to PDF

| Type | Formats |
|------|---------|
| Office | DOCX, DOC, ODT, XLSX, XLS, ODS, PPTX, PPT, ODP, TXT, RTF |
| Images | JPG, JPEG, PNG, GIF, BMP, TIFF, WEBP, SVG |
| Web and text | HTML (or a ZIP with the HTML and its CSS and images), Markdown |
| Email | EML, MSG (Outlook) |
| eBook | EPUB, MOBI, AZW3, FB2 |
| Comics | CBZ, CBR |

Image options: **Color Type** (**Color**, **Grayscale** or **Black & White**), **Fit Option** (**Maintain Aspect Ratio**, **Fit Document to Page** or **Fill Page**), **Auto Rotate**, and **Combine Images** to put all images in one PDF instead of one PDF each.

## Convert from PDF

| Type | Formats |
|------|---------|
| Office | DOCX, ODT, PPTX, ODP, XLSX, CSV |
| Text | TXT, RTF, Markdown |
| Images | PNG, JPG, GIF, TIFF, BMP, WEBP |
| Web | HTML, XML |
| Standards | PDF/A (archiving), PDF/X (print), PDF/UA (accessible) |
| eBook and comics | EPUB, AZW3, CBZ, CBR |

Notes on some targets:

- **Images** - set **Color Type**, **DPI** (72-600, default 300) and **Output**: **Multiple** (default) for one image per page, or **Single** for one image containing all pages.
- **Word, PowerPoint and Excel** - run [OCR](doc:tools/guides/ocr) on scans first.
- **PDF/A** - pick the level (default PDF/A-2b). **Strict Mode** stops with an error if the result does not fully conform. Digital signatures are removed.
- **PDF/UA** - tags the PDF for screen readers. Add a description for each image, or the file comes back tagged but not certified.

A few conversions, such as PDF to PostScript, EPS, PCL or XPS, have no option in Convert. They are available through the [REST API](doc:developers/api).

In the desktop app, some conversions need Stirling Cloud or a server ([Where your tools run](doc:desktop/where-tools-run)).

tools/guides/fill-form.title: Fill forms
tools/guides/fill-form.description: Fill in PDF forms, add or edit form fields, export form data, and detect fields automatically.
tools/guides/fill-form.markdown:
Open a PDF and select **Form Editor**, then choose a **Form editor mode**: **Fill**, **Create** or **Modify**. A PDF with no fields opens in **Create**.

## Fill in a form

1. In **Fill**, click each field on the page (or in the field list) and enter a value.
2. Turn on **Flatten after filling** to lock the answers into the page.
3. Click **Save** or press **Ctrl+S** (**Cmd+S** on a Mac) to write the values into the PDF. Required fields must be filled first.

To export the entered values, click **JSON**, **CSV** or **XLSX**. If fields don't show up correctly, click **Re-scan fields**.

## Add fields

1. Switch to **Create**.
2. Pick a field type (**Text**, **Checkbox**, **Dropdown**, **List box**, **Radio**, **Button** or **Signature**), then draw it on the page. Press **Esc** to stop drawing.
3. Click **Add *n* field(s) to PDF**.

A **Signature** field is only a placeholder that marks where a signature belongs. To sign, use [Sign](doc:tools/security/sign) or [Certificate signing](doc:tools/security/certificate-signing).

## Edit fields

In **Modify**, select a field to change its properties, drag it to a new position, or delete it. Click **Save *n* change(s)** when you're done.

## Detect fields automatically

**Auto Form Detection** finds text fields, checkboxes and signature areas in a flat PDF and makes them fillable.

1. In **Auto Form Detection**, choose a **Detection sensitivity**: **Strict**, **Balanced** (recommended) or **Thorough**.
2. Click **Detect form fields** and review the result. If nothing is found, undo, switch to **Thorough** and run it again.

If **Auto Form Detection** is greyed out, the server has no detection model or it was turned off. The ultra-lite image and the JAR downloads can't run it at all. See [Tools that are off by default](doc:server/customisation/features-and-endpoints) for the admin steps.

To lock or unlock form fields, use **Flatten** or **Unlock PDF Forms** ([Signing and security tools](doc:tools/security/security)).

tools/guides/mobile-scanner.title: Mobile scanner
tools/guides/mobile-scanner.description: Scan documents with your phone camera and send them straight into Stirling PDF with a QR code.
tools/guides/mobile-scanner.markdown:
## Scan from your phone

1. On your computer, click the QR code button (**Upload from Mobile**) next to **Add Files** (**Open Files** in the desktop app), or **From your phone** in the file picker.
2. Scan the QR code with your phone's camera and open the link.
3. Choose an upload method:
   - **Camera** - photograph each page. Edge detection finds the page and crops it for you. Use **Retake** or **Add More** as needed.
   - **File Upload** - pick existing photos on the phone.
4. Tap **Upload**. The files appear on your computer.

- **Camera** needs a secure (HTTPS) connection. If the phone says camera access requires HTTPS, use **File Upload** instead, or ask your admin to serve Stirling PDF over HTTPS.
- The QR code button is hidden when you open Stirling PDF on a phone. If you don't see it on a computer, the mobile scanner is turned off. On a self-hosted server an admin can turn it on ([Mobile scanner settings](doc:server/customisation/mobile-scanner)).

## In the desktop app

- Your phone and computer must be on the same network (Wi-Fi).
- The phone page has no edge detection or auto-crop, so crop your photos before uploading.
- The phone page also accepts PDFs.

tools/guides/ocr.title: OCR
tools/guides/ocr.description: Make scanned PDFs searchable and selectable, and clean up scans, with OCR.
tools/guides/ocr.markdown:
OCR (optical character recognition) finds the text in scanned or photographed pages and adds it to the PDF, so you can search, select and copy it.

## Run OCR

1. Select one or more PDFs and open **OCR / Cleanup scans**.
2. Under **Languages**, choose every language that appears in the document. At least one is required.
3. Pick an **OCR Mode** and any **Processing Options** (below).
4. Click **Process OCR and Review**, check the result, and download it.

## Options

**OCR Mode**

- **Auto (skip text layers)** - the default. Skips pages that already have text.
- **Force (re-OCR all, replace text)** - OCRs every page and replaces any existing text.
- **Strict (abort if text found)** - stops if any page already has selectable text.

**Processing Options**

| Option | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| **Compatibility Mode** | Makes larger files that work better with some languages and older PDF software. |
| **Create a text file** | Also saves the recognised text as a separate .txt file. |
| **Deskew pages** | Straightens tilted pages before recognition. |
| **Clean input file** | Removes noise and boosts contrast before recognition. |
| **Clean final output** | Tidies the text layer in the finished PDF. |

In the desktop app, OCR usually needs Stirling Cloud or a server ([Where your tools run](doc:desktop/where-tools-run)). On a self-hosted server, if a language is missing, ask your admin ([OCR languages](doc:server/operations/ocr-languages)).

tools/guides/page-operations.title: Page operations
tools/guides/page-operations.description: Merge, split, reorder, rotate, remove, resize and lay out the pages of your PDFs.
tools/guides/page-operations.markdown:
To edit pages visually with thumbnails, see [Workspace and Page Editor](doc:tools/workspace/page-editor).

## Merge

**Merge** joins two or more PDFs into one, in the order shown. Drag files to reorder them, or use **Sort By** (**File Name** or **Date Modified**, ascending or descending). Options:

- **Generate table of contents in the merged file?** adds clickable bookmarks named after the original files.
- **Remove digital signature in the merged file?** strips signatures, which merging breaks anyway.

**Create Portfolio** is the alternative when the files should stay separate: it bundles them into one PDF portfolio, whatever their type.

## Split

**Split** breaks one PDF into several files. Choose a method:

| Method | Splits |
|--------|--------|
| **Page Numbers** | After each page you enter. `3,7` gives pages 1-3, 4-7 and 8 to the end. A range splits after every page in it |
| **Chapters** | At each bookmark, using the document's outline |
| **Sections** | Each page into a grid of horizontal and vertical pieces, for example halves or quarters |
| **File Size** | Into parts under a maximum size, for example `10MB` |
| **Page Count** | Into files with a set number of pages each |
| **Document Count** | Into a set number of files |
| **Page Divider** | At QR code divider sheets placed between documents when scanning a batch |
| **Printable Chunks** | Each oversized page into tiles of a standard paper size (A4, Letter and so on) for printing as a poster |

## Reorder and rotate

- **Reorganize Pages** - rearrange, duplicate or delete pages. Choose an **Organization mode**, for example **Custom Page Order** (enter an order such as `1,3,2,4-6`), **Reverse Order**, **Duplex Sort** (for scans of all fronts then all backs), **Odd-Even Split**, **Odd-Even Merge** or **Duplicate all pages**.
- **Rotate** - turns all pages by 90-degree steps with **Rotate Counterclockwise** and **Rotate Clockwise**.
- **Auto Rotate** - detects each page's orientation and turns it upright, then shows a report of what it changed. **Detection method** is **Auto**, **Text only** or **OCR only**. Tick **Rotate low confidence pages to match** to turn blank or nearly blank pages the same way as the rest.

## Remove and extract pages

- **Extract Pages** - copies the pages you enter into a new PDF, in order.
- **Remove Pages** - deletes the pages you enter.
- **Remove Blank pages** - finds and removes pages with little or no content. Tick **Include detected blank pages** to also get a PDF of the removed pages so you can check them.

In **Extract Pages** and **Remove Pages**, enter single pages and ranges such as `1,3,5-8`, or expressions such as `2n-1` (odd pages).

## Page size and layout

- **Adjust page size/scale** - choose a **Target Page Size** (A0-A6, Letter, Legal or **Keep Original Size**) and a **Scale Factor** for the content. **Page orientation** (**Portrait** or **Landscape**) sets which way round the chosen size is used. It is unavailable with **Keep Original Size**.
- **Crop PDF** - drag the crop area on the preview, or click **Auto-crop whitespace**, then **Apply Crop**.
- **Multi-Page Layout** - places several pages on each sheet, in a grid of rows and columns, with optional borders.
- **PDF to Single Large Page** - stacks every page into one tall page.
- **Booklet Imposition** - reorders and lays out pages so that, printed double-sided and folded, they read in order.

## Add to pages

- **Add Page Numbers** - choose the position, which pages to number, the starting number and a custom format such as `Page {n}`. **Zero-pad Width (Bates Stamping)** pads numbers to a fixed width, for example `001`.
- **Manage Attachments** - add, extract, rename or delete files embedded in the PDF.

tools/guides/redact.title: Redact
tools/guides/redact.description: Permanently remove sensitive text and areas from a PDF, automatically or by hand.
tools/guides/redact.markdown:
Redact permanently deletes sensitive text and areas from a PDF, not just hides them. Keep a copy of the original.

## Automatic redaction

1. Under **Redaction Method**, choose **Automatic**.
2. Under **Words to Redact**, type a word or phrase and click **Add**. Repeat for each one.
3. (Optional) Under **Advanced**, set:
   - **Use Regex** - treat each entry as a regular expression.
   - **Whole Word Search** - match whole words only, so "John" doesn't match "Johnson".
   - **Box Color** and **Custom Extra Padding** - the look of the redaction boxes.
   - **Convert PDF to PDF-Image** - turns the redacted pages into images so no text at all remains behind the boxes. The text is then no longer selectable or searchable.
4. Click **Redact**.

Automatic mode can redact several files at once: select them in the file manager first.

### Patterns for personal data

With **Use Regex** on, try these patterns:

| Type | Example pattern |
| --- | --- |
| US Social Security number | `\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}` |
| Credit or debit card | `\d{4}[ -]?\d{4}[ -]?\d{4}[ -]?\d{4}` |
| IBAN | `[A-Z]{2}\d{2}[A-Z0-9]{1,30}` |
| US routing number (ABA) | `\b\d{9}\b` |
| Labelled account number | `[Aa]ccount\s*#?\s*\d{6,}` |
| Email address | `[\w.-]+@[\w.-]+\.\w+` |
| US phone number | `\(\d{3}\)\s*\d{3}-\d{4}` |
| Date (YYYY-MM-DD) | `\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}` |

## Manual redaction

1. Under **Redaction Method**, choose **Manual**. The document opens in the viewer.
2. Set the **Redaction Color**.
3. Select text, or draw an area over images, signatures or anything else, to mark it. Marks stay pending until you apply them.
4. To drop a pending mark, select it and click **Remove this mark**.
5. Apply a mark with **Apply** in its selection menu, or all pending marks with **Apply Redactions** in the panel. **Save Changes** applies any pending marks and saves the file.

tools/security/certificate-signing.title: Certificate signing
tools/security/certificate-signing.description: Sign PDFs with a digital certificate, check existing signatures and add trusted timestamps.
tools/security/certificate-signing.markdown:
A certificate signature proves who signed a PDF and shows if anyone changes it afterwards.

On a self-hosted server, an admin sets up the server certificate, which certificate authorities count as trusted, revocation checks and the allowed timestamp servers ([Signing certificates and trust](doc:server/security/signing)).

## Sign with a certificate

1. Open your PDF and pick **Sign with Certificate**.
2. In **Certificate source**, choose where the certificate comes from. This step only appears when there is more than one option.
   - **Upload** - your own certificate file.
   - **Server** - your organisation's certificate, held on the server.
   - **This device** - a certificate on your computer or a USB token. Desktop app only, see [On the desktop app](#on-the-desktop-app).
3. For **Upload**, pick the **Certificate Format**, then add your files under **Certificate Files** and enter the **Certificate Password** if there is one.

   | Format | Files |
   |---|---|
   | PKCS12 or PFX | One `.p12` or `.pfx` file |
   | PEM | A private key (`.pem`, `.der`, `.key`) and a certificate (`.pem`, `.der`, `.crt`, `.cer`) |
   | JKS | A Java keystore (`.jks`, `.keystore`) |

4. In **Signature Appearance**, choose **Invisible** or **Visible**. For a visible signature, set **Reason**, **Page Number** and **Logo** (**No Logo** or **Show Logo**). The box shows the certificate name, the date and the reason. **Name** and **Location** are saved in the signature details only.
5. Click **Sign PDF**.

Good to know:

- Expired or not-yet-valid certificates are refused.
- PDF viewers show self-signed certificates as unverified.
- For proof of when the file was signed, run [Timestamp PDF](#timestamping-pdfs) afterwards.

## On the desktop app

The desktop app can sign with a certificate in the Windows certificate store, or on a USB token or smart card (PKCS#11). This works in **Local Only** and **Stirling Cloud** mode.

1. In **Certificate source**, choose **This device**.
2. Choose the type:
   - **Windows certificate store** (Windows only) - pick a **Certificate** from the list. Windows asks for your PIN when you sign.
   - **USB Token** - pick the **PKCS#11 driver**, enter the **Token PIN**, set **Slot (optional)** if needed, then click **List certificates** and pick one.
3. Continue with **Signature Appearance** and click **Sign PDF**.

> **⚠️ Warning**
>
> Tokens lock after a few wrong PINs. Check your PIN before you click **List certificates**.


Common drivers (OpenSC, YubiKey, SoftHSM2) are found automatically. For any other driver, set the `STIRLING_PKCS11_LIBRARIES` environment variable to its full path (comma-separated for several) and restart the app.

## Validating signatures

1. Open the signed PDF and pick **Validate PDF Signature**.
2. Optional: under **Custom Certificate File X.509 (Optional)**, add a certificate (`.cer`, `.crt`, `.pem` or `.der`) to check the signatures against. It replaces the usual trusted certificate authorities for that check.
3. Click **Validate Signatures**.

Each signature gets a status:

- **Valid** - the signature is intact and the signer's certificate is trusted.
- **Valid, signer not verified** (**Unverified** in lists) - the signature is intact, but a trust check failed. The result lists why.
- **Invalid** - the cryptographic check failed.

You can download the results as a PDF report, CSV or JSON.

## Timestamping PDFs

**Timestamp PDF** adds a trusted RFC 3161 timestamp that proves the PDF existed at a point in time.

1. Open the PDF and pick **Timestamp PDF**.
2. In **Select a TSA server**, pick a Time Stamp Authority: DigiCert, Sectigo, SSL.com, FreeTSA, MeSign, or one your admin added. DigiCert is the default unless your admin changed it.
3. Click **Apply Timestamp**.

Only a hash of the document goes to the timestamp server. Existing signatures stay intact.

tools/security/security.title: Signing and security tools
tools/security/security.description: Tools for signing PDFs, protecting them with passwords and permissions, and checking or removing signatures.
tools/security/security.markdown:
In the tool picker, these tools sit under **Signing**, **Document Security**, **Verification** and **Removal**.

## Signing

- **Sign** - draw, type or upload a signature and place it on the page. See [Sign](doc:tools/security/sign).
- **Sign with Certificate** - add a digital signature that proves who signed and shows if the file is changed later. See [Certificate signing](doc:tools/security/certificate-signing).
- **Timestamp PDF** - add a trusted RFC 3161 timestamp that proves the PDF existed at a point in time. See [Timestamping PDFs](doc:tools/security/certificate-signing).

## Document security

- **Add Password** - set a **User Password** (needed to open the file) and an **Owner Password** (controls what people can do once it's open).
- **Change Permissions** - allow or block printing, copying, editing, form filling and other actions.
- **Add Watermark** - stamp text or an image across the pages.
- **Add Stamp to PDF** - add a text or image stamp at a set position. See [Content and editing](doc:tools/guides/content-editing).
- **Sanitize** - remove JavaScript, embedded files, links, metadata and fonts.
- **Flatten** - merge form fields and other interactive elements into the page so they can't be edited.
- **Unlock PDF Forms** - make read-only form fields editable again.

## Verification

- **Validate PDF Signature** - check who signed, whether their certificate is trusted and whether the file changed after signing. See [Validating signatures](doc:tools/security/certificate-signing).
- **Get ALL Info on PDF** - show the PDF version, fonts, page sizes, permissions, metadata and more, as tables or JSON.

## Removal

- **Remove Password** - unlock a protected PDF. You need the current password.
- **Remove Certificate Sign** - strip digital signatures, for example so you can edit a signed file.

To black out text or areas for good, use [Redact](doc:tools/guides/redact).

tools/security/sign.title: Sign
tools/security/sign.description: Draw, type or upload a signature and place it on a PDF with the Sign tool.
tools/security/sign.markdown:
**Sign** adds a visible signature only, which anyone can copy. To prove who signed and detect later changes, use [Sign with Certificate](doc:tools/security/certificate-signing).

## Add a signature

1. Open your PDF and pick **Sign** from the tool picker.
2. Under **Your signatures**, click **New signature** and create it on one of the tabs:
   - **Draw** - sign with a mouse, trackpad, pen or finger.
   - **Type** - type your name and pick a style. Tick **Also save my initials** to save your initials too.
   - **Upload** - add a PNG, JPG or WebP image. White backgrounds are removed automatically.
   - **Phone** - scan the QR code, sign on your phone, and the signature appears in the app.
3. Tick **Save to my signatures** to keep it, and **Make default** if you want. Click **Use signature**.
4. Click the PDF to place the signature. Place it as many times as you need, on any page. Drag a placed signature to move or resize it.
5. Click **Apply N signatures**. The signed PDF replaces the original in your workspace.

## Saved signatures

- To reuse one, pick it under **Your signatures** and click the page.
- Signed in, you can keep up to 20 signatures. Without signing in, up to 10 are kept in this browser.
- Admins can set **Who can use it** to **Everyone** to share a signature with all users. Shared signatures appear under **Shared**.

tools/tools.title: All tools
tools/tools.description: Every tool in the Stirling PDF tool picker, grouped the way the app shows them, with a link to each guide.
tools/tools.markdown:
Every tool in the app, grouped as the tool picker shows them. To find one fast, type its name in **Search tools...** at the top of the picker.

Not every tool is available everywhere. In the desktop app, tools with a cloud badge need Stirling Cloud or a server ([Where your tools run](doc:desktop/where-tools-run)). On a self-hosted server, an admin can turn tools off ([Turn features on or off](doc:server/customisation/features-and-endpoints)).

## Quick access

The most-used tools sit at the top of the picker. Each one has a keyboard shortcut ([Keyboard shortcuts](doc:tools/workspace/keyboard-shortcuts)).

- **[PDF Text Editor](doc:tools/guides/content-editing)** - edit the existing text and images in a PDF.
- **[Page Editor](doc:tools/workspace/page-editor)** (**PDF Multi Tool** in the picker) - rotate, reorder, delete, split and insert blank pages.
- **[Merge](doc:tools/guides/page-operations)** - combine several PDFs into one.
- **[Compare](doc:tools/guides/compare)** - show the text differences between two PDFs.
- **[Compress](doc:tools/guides/compress)** - make a PDF smaller.
- **[Convert](doc:tools/guides/convert)** - convert between PDF and other formats.
- **[OCR / Cleanup scans](doc:tools/guides/ocr)** - make scanned PDFs searchable and clean them up.
- **[Redact](doc:tools/guides/redact)** - permanently black out text, areas or whole pages.

## Signing

- **[Sign with Certificate](doc:tools/security/certificate-signing)** - add a digital signature that proves who signed and shows later changes.
- **[Timestamp PDF](doc:tools/security/certificate-signing)** - add an RFC 3161 timestamp that proves when the PDF existed.
- **[Sign](doc:tools/security/sign)** - add a drawn, typed or image signature.

## Document security

- **[Add Password](doc:tools/security/security)** - require a password to open the PDF and restrict what people can do.
- **[Add Watermark](doc:tools/security/security)** - put a text or image watermark across the pages.
- **[Add Stamp to PDF](doc:tools/guides/content-editing)** - add a text or image stamp at a set position.
- **[Sanitize](doc:tools/security/security)** - remove JavaScript, embedded files and other risky content.
- **[Flatten](doc:tools/security/security)** - turn form fields and other interactive parts into plain page content.
- **[Unlock PDF Forms](doc:tools/security/security)** - make read-only form fields editable again.
- **[Change Permissions](doc:tools/security/security)** - allow or block printing, copying, editing and other actions.

## Verification

- **[Get ALL Info on PDF](doc:tools/security/security)** - show the version, fonts, page sizes, permissions and metadata.
- **[Validate PDF Signature](doc:tools/security/certificate-signing)** - check who signed a PDF and whether it changed afterwards.

## Document review

- **[Read](doc:tools/workspace/read-and-annotate)** - open a PDF in the viewer to read, search, comment and mark it up.
- **[Change Metadata](doc:tools/guides/content-editing)** - edit the title, author, keywords, dates and other details.
- **[Edit Table of Contents](doc:tools/guides/content-editing)** - add, nest and reorder bookmarks.

## Page formatting

- **[Crop PDF](doc:tools/guides/page-operations)** - trim pages to the area you want.
- **[Rotate](doc:tools/guides/page-operations)** - turn pages.
- **[Auto Rotate](doc:tools/guides/page-operations)** - detect each page's orientation and turn it upright.
- **[Split](doc:tools/guides/page-operations)** - split one PDF into several files.
- **[Reorganize Pages](doc:tools/guides/page-operations)** - rearrange, duplicate or delete pages.
- **[Adjust page size/scale](doc:tools/guides/page-operations)** - change the page size and how big the content sits on it.
- **[Add Page Numbers](doc:tools/guides/page-operations)** - number pages in a set position and format.
- **[Multi-Page Layout](doc:tools/guides/page-operations)** - put several pages on each sheet.
- **[Booklet Imposition](doc:tools/guides/page-operations)** - order pages for printing and folding into a booklet.
- **[PDF to Single Large Page](doc:tools/guides/page-operations)** - join all pages into one long page.
- **[Manage Attachments](doc:tools/guides/page-operations)** - add, extract, rename or delete files embedded in the PDF.
- **[Create Portfolio](doc:tools/guides/page-operations)** - bundle several files into one PDF portfolio.

## Extraction

- **[Extract Pages](doc:tools/guides/page-operations)** - save chosen pages as a new PDF.
- **[Extract Images](doc:tools/guides/content-editing)** - save every image in the PDF to a ZIP file.

## Removal

- **[Remove Pages](doc:tools/guides/page-operations)** - delete the pages you choose.
- **[Remove Blank pages](doc:tools/guides/page-operations)** - find and drop pages with little or no content.
- **[Remove Annotations](doc:tools/guides/content-editing)** - delete all comments, highlights and markup.
- **[Remove image](doc:tools/guides/content-editing)** - strip every image, for example to shrink the file.
- **[Remove Password](doc:tools/security/security)** - unlock a protected PDF when you know its password.
- **[Remove Certificate Sign](doc:tools/security/security)** - strip digital signatures so you can edit the file.

## Automation

- **[Auto Form Detection](doc:tools/guides/fill-form)** - find form fields and make a PDF fillable.
- **[Automate](doc:tools/guides/automate)** - save a chain of tools and run it on any files.
- **[Auto Rename PDF File](doc:tools/guides/advanced-tools)** - rename a file from the title found in it.

## General

- **[Add Text](doc:tools/guides/content-editing)** - type text anywhere on a page.
- **[Add image](doc:tools/guides/content-editing)** - place an image anywhere on a page.
- **[Annotate](doc:tools/workspace/read-and-annotate)** - highlight, draw, add notes and shapes in the viewer.
- **[Form Editor](doc:tools/guides/fill-form)** - fill in, add and edit form fields.

## Advanced formatting

- **[Adjust Colors/Contrast](doc:tools/guides/advanced-tools)** - change contrast, brightness and saturation.
- **[Repair](doc:tools/guides/advanced-tools)** - try to fix a damaged PDF.
- **[Detect & Split Scanned Photos](doc:tools/guides/advanced-tools)** - find the photos on a scanned page and save each photo as a separate image.
- **[Overlay PDFs](doc:tools/guides/advanced-tools)** - lay one PDF over another.
- **[Replace & Invert Color](doc:tools/guides/advanced-tools)** - swap or invert colours, for example for high contrast.

## Developer tools

- **[Show Javascript](doc:tools/guides/advanced-tools)** - list any JavaScript inside a PDF.
- **API**, **Automated Folder Scanning**, **SSO Guide** and **Air-gapped Setup** link to the matching docs.

## AI

The AI assistant isn't in the tool list. Open it with the **Open Stirling AI assistant** button in the workspace ([AI assistant](doc:tools/guides/ai-assistant)).

tools/workspace/files-and-sharing.title: My files and sharing
tools/workspace/files-and-sharing.description: Keep files on the server with the File library, organise them in folders, and share them with other users or by link.
tools/workspace/files-and-sharing.markdown:
Login required

The **File library** keeps your files on the server and lets you share them with other users.

On Stirling Cloud, guests can't store or share files. In the desktop app, sign in to Stirling Cloud or connect to a self-hosted server. On a self-hosted server, file storage is on by default, but an admin has to turn on sharing ([File storage and sharing](doc:server/storage/file-storage)).

## Open the File library

Click **File library** in the left rail, or **Browse all files & folders** next to **PDF Library** in the file sidebar.

Use **Filter by source** to see where each file lives:

- **Cloud** - stored on the Stirling server
- **Local** - only stored in this browser
- **Shared** - shared with you by someone else

## Keep a file on the server

- From the workspace: open the file's **More actions** menu in the file sidebar and choose **Upload to server**. After you change the file, choose **Update on server** to save the new version.
- In the File library: select files and choose **Add to Stirling library…**. Files you upload or drop while a server folder is open go straight into that folder.

## Organise files

- Click **New folder**, then **New folder on the server**. Server folders are private to you.
- Open a folder's menu to **Rename** it, add a **New subfolder**, change its color and icon with **Appearance...**, or **Delete folder**.
- Drag files onto a folder in the tree on the left, or select them and choose **Move to…**.
- Open a file's **Version journey** to see earlier versions, open one in the workspace, or remove it.
- When you delete a file that's both on this device and on the server, choose **This device only**, **Cloud only** or **Everywhere**.

## Share a file

Select the file in the File library and choose **Manage sharing**, or click **Share** in the toolbar above an open file. If the file isn't on the server yet, click **Save to server & share** first.

Each person or link gets a role: **Editor** (the default), **Commenter** or **Viewer**. **Commenter** and **Viewer** can open and download the file. Only the owner can replace the file, delete it or change who has access.

### Share with a person

Under **Shared users**, enter their **Username or email** and click **Add**.

They need an account on the server you're using (on Stirling Cloud, a Stirling Cloud account). Remove access at any time with **Remove**.

### Share with a link

Pick a **Role**, click **Generate Link**, then **Copy**.

Anyone with the link must sign in before they can open it. They can then click **Open in Stirling PDF** or **Download**. Links expire after a set number of days (on a self-hosted server an admin sets this, 3 by default). To stop a link working, click **Remove link**.

To see who used a link, click **View activity**. It lists each person, whether they **Viewed** or **Downloaded** the file, and when.

tools/workspace/keyboard-shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
tools/workspace/keyboard-shortcuts.description: Default keyboard shortcuts for tools and the PDF viewer, and how to change them.
tools/workspace/keyboard-shortcuts.markdown:
On a Mac, use **⌘** for **Ctrl** and **⌥** for **Alt**.

## Tool shortcuts

The tools in the picker's Quick access list get **Ctrl + Alt + 1** to **8** by default, in list order:

| Shortcut | Tool |
|---|---|
| `Ctrl + Alt + 1` | PDF Text Editor |
| `Ctrl + Alt + 2` | PDF Multi Tool |
| `Ctrl + Alt + 3` | Merge |
| `Ctrl + Alt + 4` | Compare |
| `Ctrl + Alt + 5` | Compress |
| `Ctrl + Alt + 6` | Convert |
| `Ctrl + Alt + 7` | OCR / Cleanup scans |
| `Ctrl + Alt + 8` | Redact |

Other tools have no shortcut until you add one. Shortcuts are saved in this browser (or in the desktop app on this computer), so they don't follow you to other devices.

### Change a shortcut

1. Open **Settings → Preferences** and expand **Keyboard Shortcuts**.
2. Find the tool and click **Change shortcut**.
3. Press the new key combination, or press **Esc** to cancel.

A shortcut must include **Ctrl**, **Alt** or **⌘**. **Shift** on its own doesn't count. If another tool already uses the combination, you'll see **Shortcut already used by** and the tool's name.

To go back to the default, click **Reset**. For a tool with no default, **Reset** removes the shortcut.

## PDF viewer shortcuts

Print, select all and zoom work whenever the viewer is open. The rest work while your pointer is over the viewer.

| Shortcut | Action |
|---|---|
| `Ctrl + P` | Print |
| `Ctrl + A` | Select all text |
| `Ctrl + =` or `Ctrl + +` | Zoom in |
| `Ctrl + -` | Zoom out |
| `Ctrl + 0` | Fit to width |
| `Ctrl + F` | Open or focus search |
| `Ctrl + S` | Save changes |
| `Ctrl + Z` | Undo |
| `Ctrl + Shift + Z` or `Ctrl + Y` | Redo |
| `Home` / `End` | First / last page |
| `Page Up` / `Page Down` | Previous / next page |
| `Esc` | Close search |

With the **Rotate** tool open, press `←` to rotate left and `→` to rotate right.

## Desktop app shortcuts

| Shortcut | Action |
|---|---|
| `Ctrl + S` | Save the selected files to disk, or all files if none are selected. Files that didn't come from disk open a **Save As** dialog. |
| `Ctrl + N` | Open a new empty window (Windows and macOS only). |
| `Ctrl + R` / `Ctrl + Shift + R` | Rotate the view in the viewer clockwise / anticlockwise. |

tools/workspace/page-editor.title: Workspace and Page Editor
tools/workspace/page-editor.description: How the workspace keeps your files between tools, and how to edit pages visually in the Page Editor.
tools/workspace/page-editor.markdown:
Add your files to the workspace once, then run as many tools on them as you like. The **Page Editor** lets you edit their pages as thumbnails.

## The workspace

- Drag files onto the app or click **Add files**. They appear in the file sidebar under **PDF Library**.
- Workspace files are kept in this browser (in the desktop app, on this computer). To keep a file on the server or share it, see [My files and sharing](doc:tools/workspace/files-and-sharing).
- After a tool runs, click **Undo** to restore the files as they were.
- Each tool run saves a new version of the file. To see earlier versions, open the file's **More actions** menu in the sidebar and choose **Version history**. From there you can open an earlier version in the workspace or remove it.

## Edit pages in the Page Editor

1. Open **Page Editor** from the top bar, or pick **PDF Multi Tool** in the tool picker. Each file gets its own row of page thumbnails.
2. Select pages with their checkboxes, with **Select All**, or with **Select by Page Numbers**.
3. Change the pages:
   - Drag pages to reorder them, or drop them into another file's row.
   - Hover over a page for **Move left**, **Move right**, **Rotate left**, **Rotate right**, **Delete page** and **View page**.
   - Hover between two pages for **Split here** or **Insert blank page**.
   - For several pages at once, use **Rotate selected pages left**, **Rotate selected pages right**, **Delete selected pages**, **Insert blank pages after selected pages** or **Split after selected pages**.
4. Use **Wrap pages**, **Zoom in** and **Zoom out** to change the view, and **Undo** and **Redo** if you change your mind.
5. Click **Save changes to all files** to apply your edits.

To run the same steps on many files, use [Automate](doc:tools/guides/automate).

tools/workspace/processing-folders.title: Processing folders
tools/workspace/processing-folders.description: Turn a folder in the File library into a processing folder that runs a preset on every file you add.
tools/workspace/processing-folders.markdown:
Login required

A processing folder runs the same processing on every file you put in it, for example classifying documents ([My files and sharing](doc:tools/workspace/files-and-sharing)).

Processing folders are personal: only you can see them. Presets marked **Requires AI engine** only work when AI is available. On Stirling Cloud, processing uses your team's credits ([Plans, credits and billing](doc:cloud/plans-and-billing)).

## Set up a folder

1. Start from either place:
   - Click **Process a folder** in the left rail.
   - In the **File library**, open a folder's menu and choose **Process files in this folder...**. This skips step 2.
2. Choose the folder. Pick one under **Server storage**, or create a new one, then click **Choose processing**.
3. Pick a preset and adjust its settings ([what each preset does](doc:processor/policies/policies)).
4. Click **Enable processing**.

Files already in the folder and any you add later are processed on the server. The folder shows how many files are **Ready**, **Processing**, **Failed** or **Queued**.

## Manage a folder

Open the folder's menu in the File library:

- **Edit processing...** - change the preset or its settings, then click **Save changes**. Saving replaces the folder's current processing.
- **Pause processing** / **Resume processing** - stop and restart processing new files.
- **Retry failed files** - run failed files again.
- **Restore all originals** - put back the original of every processed file. Processing is paused until you resume it. To restore one file, use **Restore original** on that file.
- **Remove processing** - turn the folder back into a normal folder.

## In the desktop app

Sign in to Stirling Cloud or connect a self-hosted server first ([Connection modes](doc:desktop/connection-modes)).

- To use a folder on your computer, choose **On this computer** in the setup. The app watches that folder while it's running and signed in, and sends new or changed PDFs to Stirling Cloud or your server for processing.
- **Try processing your downloads folder** classifies the PDFs already in your Downloads folder and opens the results in the app. The files in Downloads aren't changed.

tools/workspace/read-and-annotate.title: Read and annotate
tools/workspace/read-and-annotate.description: Read PDFs in the viewer and add highlights, drawings, shapes, comments and notes.
tools/workspace/read-and-annotate.markdown:
Open a PDF in the viewer to read it, search it and mark it up. Two tools open the viewer:

- **Read** (under **Document Review** in the tool picker) opens the file for reading and commenting. You can also click **Reader** in the left rail.
- **Annotate** (under **General**) opens the viewer with the annotation tools in the side panel.

## Viewer

- Switch between **Single Page View** and **Dual Page View**.
- Open the **Bookmarks**, **Attachments** and **Comments** sidebars.
- Search the text, select it and click **Copy**.
- Print with **Print PDF**.

For shortcuts, see [Keyboard shortcuts](doc:tools/workspace/keyboard-shortcuts).

## Annotation tools

| Group | Tools |
|---|---|
| **Text Markup** | Highlight, Underline, Strikeout, Squiggly |
| **Drawing** | Pen, Freehand Highlighter |
| **Shapes** | Square, Circle, Line, Polygon |
| **Comments** | Comment, Insert Text, Replace Text |
| **Notes & Stamps** | Text box, Note, Add Image |

Use **Select and Edit** to move, resize or change an annotation you've placed.

To sign a PDF, use [Sign](doc:tools/security/sign) instead.

## Comments

The **Comments** sidebar lists comments by page, in reading order. From there you can:

- reply to a comment
- click **Locate in document** to jump to it
- search comments
- remove every comment with **Clear all comments** (annotations stay in the document)

## Save your changes

Click **Save Changes** or press **Ctrl + S**. Annotations are saved as standard PDF annotations that other readers can show.
